News.title: Travellers have invaded our tiny village FIVE times in 9 months – now there are no-go areas… & we’re scared of backlash
News.content:
LIVING IN FEAR Travellers have invaded our tiny village FIVE times in 9 months – now there are no-go areas… & we’re scared of backlash

FUMING locals say five traveller sites have appeared in their tiny village in just nine months, with some claiming they are now too scared to use certain roads.

Residents say the bucolic and peaceful existence in Sandway, Kent, has been ruined and blame the council for not doing enough to tackle the situation.



One resident, who asked to not be named, said: “Obviously we are not happy. It has lowered the value of our houses. It has changed the area. I won’t go down certain roads anymore.”

They added: “Residents don’t want to talk because we live here and we don’t want backlash.



“If I put my name to it they are only down the road so they could come and look into my barn.”

Locals say there are now six unauthorised sites in the immediate area, with another three authorised sites in nearby Lenham Heath.



One site in Warren Lands has been used by travellers for several years.

But residents claim five more sites have appeared within the past nine months.



The latest is near the Wishful Thinker pub and work there began in May.

Residents say they immediately reported the work to Maidstone Borough Council.

But when a council officer visited, they concluded the land had been requested for horse grazing and there had been no breach of planning permission at that stage.

Locals claim that on the next bank holiday weekend a team moved in.

They say several hedges were removed, fresh water pipes installed and a large mobile home brought onto the land.



The landowner has since submitted a retrospective planning application.

But residents say they feel they are being held to a different standard.

Sarah, 35, moved to the village just over a year ago.



She said: “It is just a bit annoying really. They just keep appearing.

“It doesn’t look very nice. Every time I walk down the road I see another one. It doesn’t seem that there is much that can be done.”

She added: “It is frustrating that I have to go through planning permission to paint my door and they can put a stonking great mobile home there and it is all fine.”

A 43-year-old man fears more sites will appear unless the council takes action, claiming they were damaging the area and having a “detrimental effect” on house prices.

He added: “Nobody wants to live here knowing that there could be more travellers moving in.



“They throw foul water out into the streets and they burn big fires. From an environmental point of view, it is very bad. It looks like a scrapyard.”

Another resident, who has lived in the area for 44 years, said: “They need to live somewhere. There aren’t any sites for them to go to, and they aren’t allowed to keep moving.

“It doesn’t bother me. I haven’t seen any problems.”



Lenham Parish Council chairman Cllr John Britt confirmed there were six sites in and around Sandway.

But he said the wider issue was the lack of a clear council policy setting out where Gypsy, Traveller and Showpeople communities could settle.

He said this was unfair to both travelling and settled communities, with the relevant local plan policy missing since the last formal assessment in 2011.

Cllr Britt said the responsibility lay with Maidstone Borough Council as the local planning authority to assess development needs and create a local plan.

A formal complaint has now been lodged by residents calling on the council to act.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Maidstone council spokesman said: “We understand the concerns raised and are investigating both the planning issues and the complaint.

“Officers are currently reviewing all available evidence before determining the most appropriate course of action and it would not be appropriate to comment further while those investigations are ongoing.”

News.title: Tragedy as teen, 19, dies after ‘getting into difficulty’ in lake at popular UK beauty spot
News.content:
LAKE HORROR Tragedy as teen, 19, dies after ‘getting into difficulty’ in lake at popular UK beauty spot

A TEENAGER has tragically died after “getting into difficulty” in a lake at a popular UK beauty spot.

Emergency responders including an air ambulance scrambled to the scene at Grasmere in the Lake District, Cumbria, at around 4.35pm yesterday.

The 19-year-old was rushed to hospital but sadly passed away, and his family have been made aware.

Cops are not treating the death as suspicious but are encouraging anyone who witnessed the incident to get in touch.





A spokesperson for Cumbria Constabulary said: “Emergency services were called at around 4.35pm yesterday (8 Aug) to Grasmere lake following reports that a young man had gotten into difficulty in the water.

“Emergency services including an air ambulance attended and a 19-year-old man was taken to hospital but has subsequently died.

“The teenager’s family have been made aware.

“Whilst the death is not being treated as suspicious, police would encourage anyone who witnessed what occurred to come forward to assist in establishing the circumstances.



“Police would also like to thank those who came to the teenager’s aid, including those who helped get him to shore.”

Anyone with information is urged to report online quoting incident number 201 of 8 August 2026 or call 101.

News.title: Woman, 31, wakes up covered in more than 100 bed bug bites in blood-stained bed after night in Travelodge hotel
News.content:
HOTEL HELL Woman, 31, wakes up covered in more than 100 bed bug bites in blood-stained bed after night in Travelodge hotel

A WOMAN woke up covered in more than 100 bed bug bites in blood-stained sheets after spending a night in a Travelodge Hotel.

Hannah Stephenson, 31, was a guest at the Newmarket Road hotel, Cambridge, when she woke up with itchy red lumps across her body.



Hannah had been out with pals in the city centre and booked a one night stop over in the hotel to save money rather than book a cab home.

But the 31-year-old woke up on July 26 to a “horrible realisation” that she had been bitten over 100 times by bed bugs.



The travel enthusiast told the BBC: “It wasn’t until I saw the blood and the bugs that I realised what had happened,’ she said.

“I woke up feeling itchy and I started to have lumps forming on my arms. When I got up, I saw spots of blood on the pillow and black dots.



“I looked closer and I actually saw a bug on the pillow. I checked the bedding and there were more in the bedding. As the day went on more and more bites started to emerge.

“I counted 37 on my left hand alone but there are too many to count, definitely more than 100, they’re really itchy.”



Hannah said she was “horrified and shocked” by the bites, which she didn’t expect from her stay at the Travelodge as she thought the company was “pretty reliable”.

Her swelling had gone down two weeks later, but she remained feeling “self conscious” as her skin looked as though she was suffering from chicken pox.

Hannah added: “People have been horrified, they’ve said I look like I have a disease. Everyone is saying how bad it looks.”



The 31-year-old said she felt “ignored” when she first complained to Travelodge, and believes the company only contacted her after she posted pictures of the bites on TikTok.

However, Travelodge said they started investigating as soon as the complaint was reported.

According to the British Pest Control Association, bed bugs are not a reflection of cleanliness or hygiene standards and are brought into environments through luggage, clothing and personal belongings.

After living in Asia, Africa and South America without experiencing bed bugs, Hannah said she would “never expect this in Cambridge”.

“I am just hoping these bites will go as soon as possible and I will look normal and get on with my life,” she added.



Hannah has accepted £2,000 in compensation from the hotel but added she hoped the company would take better precautions against bed bugs in future.

A spokesperson for Travelodge said: “We are deeply sorry for Ms Stephenson’s experience and recognise how distressing an incident like this can be.

“The safety of our customers is our priority and we maintain stringent, expert-led measures to prevent and manage pest issues, including training our housekeeping colleagues to be vigilant and to spot early signs wherever possible.

“Bed bug activity affects the wider hospitality sector and is completely unrelated to hygiene or cleanliness standards.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In the rare instance that an issue is reported in one of our hotels, we immediately take affected and surrounding rooms out of service for inspection and treatment by independent pest control experts.



“We have apologised directly to Ms Stephenson and resolved the matter to her satisfaction.”

News.title: Horror moment thug attacks girlfriend in car during two-year relationship from hell & then laughs as he’s arrested
News.content:
THIS is the moment a thug assaults his girlfriend in the car as she films him, then later laughs at the cops during his arrest.

Footage recorded on his partner’s phone shows Lee Yates, 47, peeling tape off the wingmirror as she tells him to “stop vandalising” her car.



He then orders Daisy (not her real name) to drive, before lashing out and tossing the phone from her grip, saying “do what you want”.

The phone then tumbles into the footwell as Daisy cries out “help me” and repeatedly asks Yates to give the device back.



Further bodycam footage from his subsequent arrest shows him scowling at the officer and crossing his arms defensively.

He then fronts up to the cop and sneers in her face as he denies the allegations.



Further footage, shared with The Sun, also shows him during police interview where he repeatedly says “no comment”.

The vile abuser was jailed at Lewes Crown Court on April 2 after he was found guilty of coercive and controlling behaviour.

For several years, Yates subjected Daisy to a vicious campaign of abuse, from forcing her to cook for him and dictating what she wore, a court heard.

Daisy, from Crawley, West Sussex, said: “He controlled everything in my life, from the time I woke up to the time I went to bed.

“You are scared of them and the easiest thing to do is just to abide by their rules.”



Daisy, 47, met Yates in May 2020 and said that initially he seemed nice but intense, calling her at 3am and sending her reams of messages.

She now realises he’d been love-bombing her – using excessive affection to lure her in.

After a few months had gone by, Daisy began noticing Yates’ darker side – starting with him confiscating her contraceptive pill.

“It was fine for the first four to six months and then it just started creeping up,” she said.

“He started getting angry if I wanted to stay in bed or go out with friends.”



He began controlling her wardrobe, from suggesting she change outift to demanding that she put something else on.

Yates would also time her doing house chores and would even storm in on her if she took more than three minutes in the bathroom.

Daisy said she was forced to make him meals, chauffer him around and give him money for beer.

If she refused, he would allegedly either physically assault her or threaten to kill her pet horses.

She claimed that Yates spat on her, urinated on her and threw things at her on several occasions, as well as attacked her in the car – which she fortunately caught on camera.



Daisy said: “The first time he urinated on me he said ‘I own you now.’

“He put the cold shower on my face and basically burnt my chest.

“It was hell. I physically could not do anymore. You couldn’t say no to him, it wasn’t a word he knew.”

After over two years of torment, the horror finally came to an end, after a neighbour reported Yates shoving Daisy around in the car park.

When cops arrived, Daisy told them about the abuse – realising this could be the only way to escape him.



He was arrested in July and gave a no comment interview.

Daisy said: “I was going to end up dead, I am sure I was.

“The police knocked on the door saying that someone had called. Something in my head went ‘this is your way out’.

Yates was sentenced to three years in prison on April 15 at Lewes Crown Court.

He was also charged with raping her twice but was found not guilty.



Daisy said her diaries provided a useful record of the abuse when giving evidence in court.

She explained how his vile behaviour has had a lasting impact on her and that she still lives in fear, triggered by loud noises or people drinking alcohol.

“When the police arrested him I still felt like I would get in trouble for doing things. Even now there is still stuff that triggers me,” she said.

“I will never be the same again, but I am not letting him win. There is life after trauma.

“I will never let a man treat me like that again.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking after Yates was sentenced Hannah Lane, an investigator at Sussex Police, said: “Lee Yates sought to control almost every aspect of this victim’s life, using violence and intimidation to try and subdue her.

“But he underestimated her strength. Thanks to her reporting his crimes to the police, he is now safely behind bars while she can look to rebuild her life.”

News.title: Amanda Knox’s ex-boyfriend hits out at controversial Edinburgh Fringe comedy show
News.content:
AMANDA Knox’s ex-boyfriend has hit out at her controversial Edinburgh Fringe show.

Raffaele Sollecito, 42, was wrongfully convicted alongside Knox for the 2007 murder of Meredith Kercher in Perugia, Italy, before being acquitted.



He has since joined the line of critics blasting his ex’s show Cartwheel – running for eleven nights at the Gilded Balloon.

A petition launched by a friend of the Kercher family claims that Amanda’s show turns her rape and murder into “entertainment”.



It has since been signed by over 37,000 people.

The computer engineer revealed he was “puzzled” that the murder probe was being used “as a draw for a comedy show.”



He told the Mail on Sunday: “I haven’t seen it, so I cannot pass judgement on its content. However, based on how it has been presented and promoted, I find it puzzling that a tragedy is being used as a draw for a comedy show.

“Personally, it is not an approach I agree with. I am trying to process and move past what happened in a different way.

“I don’t believe there is a right or wrong recipe for dealing with trauma; everyone finds their own path.”

We previously told how Knox, 38, joked about “dry-humping” and dismissed murder trial evidence as “just vibes” in her controversial Fringe debut.



She addressed several moments in the case – including the kiss with Raffaele outside the crime scene.



Knox said: “Even if I had been dry-humping his leg while making awkward eye contact with the lead detective, that would make me in heat, but it wouldn’t have made me a murderer.”

And on her Foxy Knoxy nickname, given to her by school friends and later picked up by the newspapers, she argued: “Even If my nickname were murder pussy, it wouldn’t make me a murderer.”

She added that the cartwheel she was alleged to have done while in police custody was in fact the splits – which is “a lot harder than a cartwheel”.

The murder of Meredith Kercher November 1, 2007 – The murder of Meredith Kercher: British exchange student Meredith Kercher, 21, is found dead in the apartment she shares with Amanda Knox in Perugia, Italy. Her throat is slashed, and signs suggest she may have been sexually assaulted. November 6, 2007 – Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito arrested: Amanda Knox, her Italian boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito, and Patrick Lumumba, Knox’s boss at a local bar, are arrested in connection with Kercher’s murder. Knox accuses Lumumba of the killing during a police interrogation. November 20, 2007 – Patrick Lumumba released: Lumumba is released after police find no forensic evidence linking him to the murder. He was falsely implicated by Knox during a contentious interrogation. December 6, 2007 – Rudy Guede arrested in Germany: Rudy Guede, a 20-year-old Ivorian man, is arrested in Germany and extradited to Italy. His DNA is found on Kercher’s body and at the crime scene. October 28, 2008 – Guede convicted of murder: Guede opts for a fast-track trial and is convicted of Kercher’s murder. He is sentenced to 30 years in prison, later reduced to 16 on appeal. January 16, 2009 – Knox and Sollecito trial begins: Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito stand trial for the murder of Kercher. Prosecutors allege a sex game gone wrong, while the defence argues that Guede acted alone. December 4, 2009 – Knox and Sollecito convicted: Knox and Sollecito are found guilty. Knox is sentenced to 26 years in prison; Sollecito receives 25 years. November 24, 2010 – Appeals process begins: Knox and Sollecito appeal their convictions. A key focus is the forensic evidence, including DNA found on a knife and a bra clasp. October 3, 2011 – Knox and Sollecito acquitted: An appeals court overturns their convictions, citing errors in the forensic investigation. Knox is freed and returns to Seattle. March 26, 2013 – Italy’s Supreme Court orders retrial: Italy’s Court of Cassation annuls the acquittals, ordering a retrial for Knox and Sollecito. January 30, 2014 – Knox and Sollecito reconvicted: Knox and Sollecito are reconvicted in their retrial. Knox, now in the U.S., is sentenced to 28.5 years in prison. March 25, 2015 – Final acquittal: Italy’s Supreme Court definitively acquits Knox and Sollecito of Kercher’s murder, citing lack of evidence and glaring errors in the investigation. November 2021 – Rudy Guede released: Rudy Guede, the sole person definitively convicted in connection with Kercher’s death, is released from prison after serving 13 years. 2023 – present – Knox’s slander conviction: Despite her acquittal, Knox is convicted of slander for falsely accusing Patrick Lumumba. 2023: The European Court of Human Rights rules that Knox’s rights were violated during her 2007 interrogation. June 2024: An Italian court upholds her slander conviction, a decision confirmed by Italy’s high court in January 2025.

Meredith’s sister Stephanie Kercher backed the petition to stop the show and said said she “could not fathom” how rape and murder could be the subject of a comedy gig.



She added: “Imagine 20 years after Meredith’s death, your pain is turned into someone else’s laughter.

“My sister’s tragedy is being used to debut a comedy show this weekend in Edinburgh of all places by the very person who was questioned and taken to the legal system by Italian prosecution.

“I’m very aware that in high profile cases everyone has their own opinions on guilt and innocence and I also agree with freedom of speech.

“However, when someone is still using Meredith’s name to support themselves, and furthermore, when a comedy is linked to an individual case and individual person.

“I cannot fathom how rape and murder can be laughed about and I cannot understand how one person’s behaviour at the police station can be the subject of the comedy show.”



But the Edinburgh Fringe has come to the defence of Knox’s show, saying they are not afraid of controversy.

Tony Lancaster, the director of the Fringe Society, told BBC Radio Scotland: “We’re not afraid of controversy.

“The decision as to whether or not (the show) goes ahead lies with Amanda herself and it lies with the venue.

“Those are conversations that they can have, but as far as I’m concerned, I believe that if you are opening up a stage and calling it an open access festival and inviting people in to tell their stories, you have to be prepared for some controversy – it’s going to happen.

“As sympathetic as we are to individual cases that crop up, and absolutely as a parent, I can relate to the pain that they describe, but that can’t be a criteria, it can’t be one of the lenses that we look through.”



Knox has also previously defended her Fringe show amid the backlash.

She posted to Instagram: “Cartwheel is a show about motherhood, raising a daughter in a world that is unfair and dangerous for women, and what it costs to be the kind of mother who tells her the truth about that.

“Neither the author of this petition nor anyone who signed it has seen Cartwheel.

“The petition contains many false assumptions and completely mischaracterises the show.

“Cartwheel honours Meredith Kercher’s memory and calls out the violence that was done to her and to me.



“A petition to cancel a show no one has seen on the grounds of false accusations intended to shame and vilify a wronged woman into silence is not an argument against Cartwheel.

“It’s a fairly precise description of what Cartwheel is about and why it deserves to exist.

“And the Edinburgh Fringe is the perfect place for a show like this.”

Leeds University exchange student Meredith, 21, from Croydon, South London, was found dead in the flat in Perugia, Umbria, she shared with Knox, now 38.

She had been raped, beaten and had her throat slit.



Knox and then-boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito were convicted of the 2007 killing and sexually assaulting Meredith in what was called a “sex game gone wrong”.

Their convictions were overturned and she received a definitive acquittal in 2015.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

­Ivorian migrant Rudy Guede served 16 years for the crimes.

Knox is now married with two children in the US.

News.title: Influencer fighting for her life after horror motorbike crash on holiday in Bali as her family issue urgent appeal
News.content:
HOLS HORROR Influencer fighting for her life after horror motorbike crash on holiday in Bali as her family issue urgent appeal

AN INFLUENCER is fighting for her life after suffering a serious motorbike crash while on holiday in Bali.

Lis Santos Bayir was rushed to hospital following the horror smash and is currently in a stable condition, according to doctors.



The Brazilian social media star was riding a motorbike when the crash happened on the Indonesian island.

She is now being treated in intensive care at BIMC Kuta Hospital in Bali.



Bayir, whose real name is Elisangela Aparecida dos Santos, has more than 18,000 followers on Instagram, where she regularly shares content about wellbeing, mental health and personal growth.

Her family issued an urgent appeal for B+ blood donations as she remained in intensive care.



In a statement, they said: “We urgently need donations of type B+ blood.

“Anyone who can donate or share this request will make a huge difference to her recovery.



“She continues under intensive care in the ICU, closely monitored by a dedicated and attentive medical team.”

Following key blood donations, her family said Bayir was responding well and is now due to undergo surgery.

They added: “The focus now is to monitor how she responds in the coming days to this new phase of stimulation.

“We remain very confident and deeply grateful for every prayer, message and positive energy sent by you.”

Her businessman husband, Ahmet Bayir, also shared a heartfelt message.



He wrote: “I know you will smile like that again and light up the world with your beautiful energy once more.

“You are stronger than you imagine, and I know you will rise again.”

No further details about the circumstances of the motorbike crash have been released.

This comes after a British tourist was killed in a motorcycle crash in Bali while celebrating his birthday with pals in June.

Joseph O’Sullivan, 26, had travelled to Indonesia from his home in Perth, Australia, where he had been living and working as a roofer for almost two years.



His death was announced by his sister Patricia O’Sullivan on Facebook on Friday.

“Just to let everyone know that my little brother Joseph has sadly passed away in a tragic accident,” she wrote.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are all in shock, love him very much, can’t believe he gone. RIP Joseph, my little brother.”

Tributes were paid to Joseph, describing him as a “brilliant lad” who had a smile “that would light up every room.”

News.title: Mystery as man fighting for his life after being found on zebra crossing outside library in popular UK seaside town
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

COP PROBE Mystery as man fighting for his life after being found on zebra crossing outside library in popular UK seaside town

A MAN is fighting for his life in hospital after being found with serious injuries on a zebra crossing.

The victim was discovered on the road early yesterday morning as cops launch an urgent probe into how he was hurt.



He was found on the zebra crossing next to Paignton Library at around 5.20am on Saturday, August 8.

Paramedics called police after coming across the badly injured man.



He was rushed to hospital where his injuries are believed to be life-threatening.

Cops are now trying to work out exactly how he came to be injured in the road.

A road closure remains in place while enquiries continue.

The man is described as white, around 6ft tall and with short hair.

He was wearing a navy zip-up hoodie, a navy polo shirt, dark grey shorts, black trainers and a black watch.

Cops are appealing for anyone who witnessed what happened or may have relevant footage to come forward.



Anyone with information is asked to call 101 or visit the force website, quoting log 184 of August 8.

News.title: Putin ‘could resort to using nuclear weapons’ as tyrant is poised to ‘mobilise half million men in weeks’ in WW3 threat
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin could resort to using nuclear weapons, a top Nato chief has warned – as the dictator is poised to prime half a million troops.

The tyrant has sparked World War Three fears with the rumoured mass mobilisation – and is keen to claw back control after suffering a string of powerful Ukrainian attacks deep inside Russia.



The chilling claim that he could resort to nuclear force came from Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, who has met the Kremlin dictator and other senior Russian officials in the past two months.

He said: “When a war of attrition at the front turns into attrition in the rear, the question is no longer whether to lose the war, but whether you will continue to exist as a nation. You use the last resort you have.





“During my visit to Russia, it seemed that this issue could be raised, as there was talk that the public is demanding something of the sort.

“We have discussed this with Western partners, and they are aware of it as well. This is a dangerous situation.



“Everything that people say will not happen ultimately does happen.”

The stark warning came as Volodymyr Zelensky claimed Putin is rumoured to mobilise half a million new soldiers within weeks in a terrifying threat to Ukraine and the West.

His aim would not only be to swell Russia’s forces against Kyiv, but also to pile psychological pressure on Nato amid fears of widening the war.

Zelensky quoted Putin as saying that there is “no guarantee that I will use these half a million only in Ukraine“.



He claimed to have intelligence on the dictator’s plans for a massive stealth mobilisation following Russian parliamentary elections in late September.

Zelensky said: “He is thinking about how to deceive his people. He will carry out a mass mobilisation without officially declaring it.”

Russians could be duped into signing “shady contracts” for supposedly safe work away from the frontline before being sent into his meat-grinder units.

Those of military age could also be stopped from travelling abroad as Putin moves to “block the borders”, preventing them from fleeing.



Zelensky said: “We are already seeing many of these steps.”

He added that the mass mobilisation would be designed to exert psychological pressure on European countries and fuel WW3 fears.

Zelensky suggested the Kremlin could use the threat of a wider conflict to deter Western nations from backing Ukraine and reduce support for Kyiv.

“We need to have a general understanding of what’s happening with the Russians to understand that they will resort to anything,” he told a United News telethon.

“There will be hundreds, even thousands, of cyberattacks, the use of missile strikes, intimidation tactics, and so on.



“Why? Because Putin cannot yet find a victory in this war.

“He needs to sell a victory. But there will be no victory for him in Ukraine.

“He needs to seize the Donbas region. We are not going to withdraw on our own.”

As well as mobilising half a million men, Putin is reportedly bringing in up to 50,000 North Korean fighters.

The warnings came amid savage overnight missile and drone strikes against Ukrainian civilians.



Russia blew apart an apartment building in Kharkiv, killing at least two people and injuring 13.

Major Ihor Terekhov said: “There are people trapped in the building, and a rescue operation has been launched at the scene.”

New Russian Banderol missiles were reportedly used.

In Odesa, residential blocks and historic buildings were hit by dozens of ballistic missiles and drones, triggering fires and injuring at least eight.

Ukraine’s depleted air defence systems were exposed as the barrage struck the Black Sea city without a single missile being intercepted.



Earlier, Ukraine struck the Black Sea resort of Gelendzhik, just 15 miles from Putin’s £1 billion clifftop palace, hitting a military unit compound.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Plumes of smoke rose over Gelendzhik as sirens sounded and tourists were ordered to immediately leave all beaches.

The FSB military plays a role in guarding Putin’s sprawling Black Sea palace, which has been likened to the lair of a James Bond villain.

News.title: Rules if an NHS dentist removes you from their patient list
News.content:
Rules if an NHS dentist removes you from their patient list

Healthwatch England has warned that millions of people are unaware of the rules around NHS dental registration

View 3 Images Patients are free to visit any NHS dentist willing to take them on (Image: Olena Miroshnichenko via Getty Images)

Millions of patients are mistakenly under the impression they hold a permanent place with their NHS dentist once they sign up.

‌



Healthwatch England has cautioned that the reality is far different, warning that surgeries can stop seeing patients once their treatment concludes and they may even remove them following repeated missed appointments. The watchdog's own research revealed that 68% of people wrongly believe they can permanently register with an NHS dentist in the same way they do with a GP.

‌



However, since reforms to the NHS dental contract in 2006, there has been no formal registration system for NHS dentists in England. Instead, patients are taken on for a course of treatment. Once that treatment concludes, the formal arrangement comes to an end, although many practices opt to maintain informal lists of regular patients and invite them back for routine check-ups.

‌



View 3 Images Healthwatch England is supporting calls for a return to GP-style registration (Image: mediaphotos via Getty Images)

Patients are free to visit any NHS dentist willing to take them on, regardless of where they live, as long as the practice is accepting NHS patients. These findings emerge against the backdrop of an ongoing shortage of NHS dental appointments, with increasing numbers of patients either unable to find a dentist or left with no option but to go private.

Healthwatch's polling revealed:.

‌



33% of people said they had waited longer than they wanted for NHS dental treatment.

16% said they had been unable to find an NHS dentist willing to treat them.

27% said they had paid for private dental care during the past two years because they could not access NHS treatment.

The problems stem in part from the way dentists are paid under the NHS contract introduced in 2006. Rather than receiving payment based on the number of registered patients, dentists are remunerated using "Units of Dental Activity" (UDAs) for completing treatments.

Many dentists contend that the system fails to provide adequate funding, prompting growing numbers to cut back their NHS work or move to private practice. According to the British Dental Association, despite the overall number of dentists rising by around 3%, only 23% now say the majority of their work is for the NHS, down from 40% before the pandemic.

‌



You could lose NHS treatment after missed appointments

Patients should also be aware that many NHS dental practices operate "failed to attend" policies. While policies differ between practices, surgeries may refuse to continue providing NHS treatment if patients repeatedly fail to turn up to appointments or regularly cancel at short notice.

For instance, some practices state they may stop treating an NHS patient after two missed appointments within two years, four short-notice cancellations, or a combination of both. Patients are ordinarily warned before this occurs, and practices typically request at least 24 to 48 hours' notice if an appointment needs to be cancelled.

View 3 Images Many practices keep informal patient lists (Image: miljko via Getty Images)

‌



Calls for reform

Healthwatch England is supporting calls for a return to GP-style registration, arguing that patients should once again have the right to remain permanently registered with an NHS dental practice for both routine and urgent care.

The Government is currently in talks with the British Dental Association over reforms to the NHS dental contract, and has launched a recruitment drive designed to boost the number of NHS dentists in areas where access to appointments is most limited.

In the meantime, Healthwatch is calling on dental practices to be more transparent with patients about the fact that they are not permanently registered with an NHS dentist, and to clearly outline what steps are needed to remain a regular NHS patient.

Article continues below

Your NHS dentist rights

You cannot formally register with an NHS dentist in England as you do with a GP.

You can attend any NHS practice that is accepting new NHS patients.

Your NHS arrangement usually ends once your course of treatment has been completed.

Many practices keep informal patient lists, but they are not legally required to do so. Repeated missed appointments or short-notice cancellations may result in a practice deciding not to offer you further NHS treatment, in line with its policy.

News.title: Trafficking survivor pleads with Shabana Mahmood to pause 'devastating' asylum change
News.content:
Trafficking survivor pleads with Shabana Mahmood to pause 'devastating' asylum change

EXCLUSIVE: Charities warn that a new streamlined interview process - which means asylum cases with little chance of success can be dismissed faster - will mean torture survivors are at greater risk of being wrongly deported

View 2 Images Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood faces calls to pause a new streamlined interview process (Image: Dan Kitwood/PA Wire)

Controversial asylum fast-tracking rules mean torture and trafficking survivors are at greater risk of being wrongly sent back to danger, Shabana Mahmood has been warned.

‌



The Home Secretary faces calls to pause a streamlining of the interview process which means some people only get one opportunity to make their case. Campaigners say traumatised victims often need more time to open up about what they have gone through.

‌



One trafficking survivor told The Mirror the changes will be "devastating" for people like him. The Helen Bamber Foundation and Freedom From Torture have called on the Home Office to rethink the new system, which came into effect on August 3.

‌



The Home Office says it will be able to identify cases that are unlikely to succeed without multiple assessments. But the charities claim this will lead to flawed decisions and lead to further appeals further down the line. They also fear most asylum seekers will have no access to legal advice before their screening interview - meaning it is very unlikely they will understand the process and what they need to do.

MP Rupert Lowe skewered as he flaps over whether King Charles is a white British man READ MORE :

Terrorism referrals rocket as children account for one in three cases READ MORE :

View 2 Images Charities warn the new regulations will lead to a rise in wrongful refusals (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Kamena Dorling, director of policy at the Helen Bamber Foundation, said: "You cannot expect a survivor of torture or trafficking to disclose the most painful experiences of their life in a single interview. Many people arrive in the UK terrified, traumatised and deeply distrustful of authority. For survivors, disclosure is often a gradual process that takes place over weeks or months, not hours.

‌



"These changes risk creating a system where people are refused before they have had a real opportunity to explain what happened to them or provide evidence of the harm they have suffered.”

Under the new rules, laid before Parliament in July, some asylum claims will be determined without a separate substantive refugee interview. Both charities have written to the Parliament's Secondary Legislation Scrutiny Committee saying the new system could increase the risk of wrongful refusals.

Sile Reynolds, from Freedom from Torture, said: “The government should be capable of deciding asylum claims more quickly – it’s in no-one’s interest for survivors to be stuck in a backlog, unable to heal, work and move on with life. But the safety of the process and the quality of the decision must not be sacrificed in the pursuit of speed, or we run the risk of sending refugees back to torture and persecution.

‌



"The government is already getting it wrong in too many cases leading to an outrageous backlog at the appeal courts. We all want to see an end to the chaos and harm inflicted on those seeking sanctuary in the UK but this must not be at the expense of fairness and justice.”

And Chris, a survivor of trafficking supported by Helen Bamber Foundation, said: "Based on my own experience as a survivor of trafficking, these changes would be devastating. They would close the window for some people seeking asylum to tell the truth about what has happened to them.

"We are human beings, and before we can talk about our trauma, we need to feel safe and be able to trust the person asking the questions. The first interview happens very soon after arriving in a new country, when you don't know anyone or understand what will happen next.

Article continues below

"Many survivors are living with trauma, memory loss, fear and shame. You cannot switch off that trauma on demand. It takes time to build enough trust to speak about experiences like trafficking and exploitation, and many people only feel able to disclose what happened little by little."

A Home Office spokesman said: “We would reassure victims and survivors of these horrific experiences that their asylum claims will continue to be examined under the standard process.

“Merged registration is only intended for a limited number of claims from safe countries, where there is no realistic prospect of a claim being granted. This will help deliver quicker decisions, reduce lengthy periods of uncertainty, and ensure protection is granted swiftly to those who genuinely need it.”

News.title: Doctors thought boy's tumours were bruises from bullies - now his best friend is trying to keep him alive
News.content:
Doctors thought boy's tumours were bruises from bullies - now his best friend is trying to keep him alive

EXCLUSIVE: Masion Turner-Potter, 11, has a 20 per cent chance of survival but his best friend Oscar Steers is raising thousands to explore potentially life-saving treatment options

View 6 Images Oscar Steers is determined to help save his best friend Masion Turner-Potter (Image: milesformasion/Instagram)

A young boy left broken when he was told his best friend has stage four cancer has raised more than £65,000 to help him get better - after doctors originally dismissed his tumours as bruising from cruel bullies.

‌



Masion Turner-Potter is fighting for his life after he was diagnosed with Rhabdomyosarcoma, a rare and aggressive form of cancer, two months ago. He is currently under-going gruelling chemotherapy after medics finally discovered a mass in his leg. Further tests showed the cancer had spread to the 11-year-old's groin, chest and spine.

‌



His family had to battle for answers after being told the marks on their son's body were down to being picked on, and they soon discovered the harrowing news that he has just a 20 per cent chance of survival.

‌



While, of course, Masion and his family's ordeal is front and centre of the minds of everyone in Chichester, West Sussex, cancer doesn't just impact those that it directly strikes.

6 View 6 Images Masion, 11, is back in hospital as he fights for life (Image: milesformasion/Instagram) 6 View 6 Images The little lads have been best friends for five years (Image: milesformasion/Instagram)

‌



Little Oscar Steers, 10, moved to the area from Chertsey, Surrey, when he was five years old and straight away forged an incredible bond with Masion, who he met on his first day of school. His world has been turned upside down by his best mate's battle - so he decided he had to do something to help.

With the support of his mum Ellie, Oscar set about trying to raise £1,000 via his JustGiving page by running a mile every day for 30 days and hoped locals would sponsor him, with all money raised enabling Masion to find the best potentially life-saving treatment available.

He smashed his target within minutes as well-wishers backed his fight to help keep his friend alive. Now he's thinking about what else he can do so they can explore costly groundbreaking treatment only available overseas.

‌



View 6 Images Maison has been diagnosed with Rhabdomyosarcoma, a rare and aggressive form of cancer (Image: milesformasion/Instagram)

Oscar told us: "Masion was my very first friend when I moved school, so he’s always been really special to me. When I found out how poorly he was, I just wanted to do something to help him.

"I love knowing that Masion watches my videos and smiles because that makes me happy too. I know I can’t make him better, but if I can make him smile and show him how many people care about him, that means so much to me. I’m sad my 30 days are over, but this isn’t the end. I will always help Masion and always be there for him. I love him so much!"

‌



His mum Ellie said the cute pair's friendship was born on their first day at school and they have been inseparable ever since. They are thankful the school pressured the hospital into looking into Masion's struggling health after his parents' concerns were ignored.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"Oscar didn't know anyone in this area when we moved here, Masion was his first friend," she said. "They are both very quiet boys, and have remained so close ever since. He has never forgotten that he's the one who made him feel so welcome. He was his friend when he didn't know anyone.

‌



"He said his body hurt. They [the doctors] thought his pain was due to the bullies and the bruises they had left on his body - they refused him so many times. Because Masion also has autism, they said he was just showing autistic traits and refused to look into it.

"It was the school who pushed the matter, saying he was not acting like a normal child should, his breathing was off and he wasn't right. The hospital said they're only going to look into this as his school had said something. That's when they found out he had stage four cancer and he had tumours all over his body. They're doing everything they can and we're all keeping as positive as possible for them."

6 View 6 Images Masion's friends are all teaming up to help his fight for life (Image: milesformasion/Instagram) 6 View 6 Images Oscar is now thinking up more money-making ideas! (Image: milesformasion/Instagram)

‌



Oscar wanted to do something and thanks to the power of social media, his 30-day Miles For Masion challenge has grown legs.

He's had pledges from all around the world after doing more than a marathon inside a month and with more ideas being talked about, there could be even more fundraising to come.

"Oscar doesn't like running, just like his mum!" Ellie said. "So to do it in the middle of not one but two heatwaves, and for him to want to be out there doing it everyday, just makes us so proud.

‌



"His heart hurts in a way no child's should. I just made the page so it would give Masion something to watch and so he would smile. But overnight it just blew up.

"He knows enough about what's going on. His friends have mobile phones, we've tried to shield him from it as much as we can. He actually said to me 'mummy I know you want to protect me, but I want you to be honest with me' so I have made that promise to him. It's so incredibly hard to navigate."

Rhabdomyosarcoma is a type of soft tissue sarcoma which usually only impacts young children and sometimes teenagers. It’s more common in boys than girls. It usually forms in the head, neck, bladder, or genital areas.

‌



"We're explaining things to a ten-year-old that you really shouldn't have to," the mum said.

"The good news is that the chemo he is on is working, but there are a number of tumours they are really concerned about. There's one on his spine that could paralise him. He's not responding well to the chemo, he is really struggling and he is back in hospital now.

"He should be out playing football and making memories on holiday, not in hospital and not living in fear. Oscar knows one mile a day is nothing compared to the fight Masion is facing - we say just prove those statistics wrong."

‌



Masion's mum Karren is thankful her son has such an incredible support network - and an amazing friend like Oscar.

"The last seven weeks have turned our world completely upside down," she said. "To go from Masion having a limp to finding out he has stage 4 rhabdomyosarcoma is something no family could ever expect or be prepared for.

"We are so incredibly grateful for Oscar and his family. What they have done for Masion has brought so much happiness during a time when the world can feel like such a dark place. I could never put into words how grateful and loved they have made us feel.

Article continues below

"Our family love watching Oscar’s videos, and Masion loves watching them too. Seeing his smile and knowing he is thinking of Masion means more to us than they will ever know."

To donate to the cause, visit Oscar's JustGiving page here.

News.title: Banksy street art cost taxpayer nearly £150,000, with bill expected to rise
News.content:
Banksy street art cost taxpayer nearly £150,000, with bill expected to rise

Local authorities and a government department said artworks by the elusive street artist Banksy have set them back thousands of pounds in fees

View 4 Images Banksy's work outside the Royal Courts of Justice has set back the MoJ around £85,000 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Three iconic street artworks by Banksy have reportedly cost the public a staggering £150,000 in cleaning and security fees.

‌



The elusive artist, thought to be from Bristol, is known for his graffiti murals that often pop up overnight and they attract large crowds. Despite all the people who come to visit these murals, some councils and a government department have been forced to spend thousands of pounds in taxpayer money in security and cleaning fees.

‌



A mural on the side of the Royal Courts of Justice has set back the Department of Justice a staggering £85,000 so far in security fees and clean up efforts.

‌



View 4 Images Security protecting the Royal Courts of Justice artwork, in September 2025 (Image: Getty Images)

The artwork depicts a protester lying on the floor, with blood on their placard, while they are being hit by a judge wielding a gavel. The mural popped up in September 2025 and was quickly covered by metal barriers and large plastic sheets.

The MoJ said £50,000 has been spent so far trying to remove the artwork from the Grade II-listed central London court and an extra £35,300 on security fees and overtime, according to a Freedom of Information request by the BBC.

‌



A HM Courts and Tribunals Service spokesperson told the Mirror: "The Royal Courts of Justice is a listed building and HMCTS are obliged to maintain its original character."

View 4 Images The Banksy statue of a man holding a flag appeared in April 2026 (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

Another Banksy artwork that led to a big bill for the taxpayer was a statue of a man carrying a flag which covered his face, on a plinth in Waterloo Place, near Trafalgar Square.

‌



Westminster City Council, which owns the land the statue was placed, said it has forked out around £60,000 on a safety barrier around the art, after it was erected in April 2026. That money has also been spent on admin fees and a security guard. Banksy, in Instagram videos, took responsibility for the statue. The Mirror has reached out to the council for comment.

View 4 Images Banksy painted a City of London police box with pictures of piranhas in 2024 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A third Banksy work that set the authorities back was a police sentry box in the City of London, which was sprayed with images of piranhas in 2024. The police box had been on Ludgate Hill since the 1990s, in response to IRA attacks across London at the time.

Article continues below

The box was removed after it was painted and this set back the City of London £2,200. The police box was removed from the street and will be exhibited at the new London Museum with it reopens later this year. The Mirror has reached out to the City of London for comment.

News.title: At least 27 injured after exploding firework shoots into beach crowd near Benidorm
News.content:
At least 27 injured after exploding firework shoots into beach crowd near Benidorm

'Real panic' broke out on the Spanish beach as the exploding rocket shot into the crowd

Many injured after exploding firework shoots into crowd near Benidorm

At least 27 people have been injured with 14 taken to hospital after an exploding firework shot into a crowd on a beach in Spain.

‌



The rocket was let off over the sea, near Benidorm on the Costa Blanca, in the early hours of Sunday as part of a huge local celebration when it veered into the crowd lining the beach front at Altea.

‌



Emergency services scrambled to the scene to evacuate and treat the injured, with 14 rushed to hospital in Alicante, 11 of whom were treated in the Burns Unit of the General University Hospital, while a further 13 were rushed to the Altea health centre.

‌



One witness said: "What was supposed to be a night of partying ended in moments of real panic. The fires went straight to the area where we were on the beach and people started running.

View Image An exploding firework has injured at least 27 people in Spain (Image: TikTok / @fredyrilo)

‌



"Ambulances and emergency services went to the scene. There is talk of numerous wounded."

Horrifying footage shows the 'peacock' rockets exploding over the ocean until one spirals out of control and directly into the crowd. A large white plume of smoke is seen while onlookers could be heard screaming in panic.

The major display is a huge prestigious pyrotechnic festival in the local calendar, held annually in Altea with fireworks fired entirely from the sea using floating platforms and barges. This year, it was held in celebration of the 40th anniversary of the Castell de l'Olla de Altea, with around 100,000 people, including locals and tourists, in attendance.

Article continues below

Organisers, the Brotherhood of Castell de l'Olla, said emergency crews rushed to help the injured, reports the Daily Star.

More details are yet to be confirmed.

News.title: EastEnders star struggles to get work a year after being axed - despite making show history
News.content:
EastEnders star struggles to get work a year after being axed - despite making show history

The actor revealed things have been tough work wise since he left the BBC soap

View 4 Images Matthew starred as Tara Misu, EastEnders first ever drag queen (Image: BBC)

Former EastEnders star Matthew James Morrison has candidly admitted he has no work lined up a year after leaving the BBC soap. The actor played Felix Baker for three years and made history during his time in Walford as the man behind Tara Misu, EastEnders' first regular drag queen character.

‌



Matthew left Albert Square in 2025 after soap bosses decided to write Felix out of the show, and while he has landed theatre roles since his departure, he has now found himself facing an uncertain future.

‌



Speaking on the Missleighdingfortunes podcast, hosted by drag performer Miss Leigh Ding, Matthew opened up about his career while having a tarot card reading.

‌



View 4 Images Matthew starred in EastEnders as Felix for three years (Image: BBC/Jack Barnes/Kieron McCarron)

Reflecting on leaving EastEnders, he said: "I finished EastEnders and I thought you know, maybe something will come, maybe something might not come.

"For a lot of people who’ve left the show since I started, some of them have worked, some of them haven’t worked."

‌



Matthew initially kept busy after leaving Walford, landing a theatre role in Greenwich, south east London, before heading into another stage production.

However, after recently finishing a tour, the actor admitted he is now without another job to move on to.

He said: "This is the first time since really leaving EastEnders – I finished the tour over a week ago – and I don’t have anything lined up.

‌



"It feels like I am stood in the desert just being like what do I do next?"

View 4 Images Matthew appeared on Miss Leighding Fortunes podcast (Image: tiktok/@missleighdingfortunes)

Matthew then pondered what his next move could be, suggesting he could use the downtime to develop new skills, including learning to ride a horse or mastering another accent.

‌



His admission comes around a year after it emerged that bosses had decided to call time on Felix's stint in Walford.

At the time, a source said: "It’s never an easy decision for bosses when they have to make the decision for a character to leave.

"Matthew has been great, but bosses felt the time was right to say goodbye to Felix."

‌



Matthew joined EastEnders as part of the Baker family, alongside Felix's father Avery and brother Finlay.

View 4 Images Matthew's character was written out of the soap a year ago (Image: BBC/Jack Barnes/Kieron McCarron)

Avery died shortly after the family's arrival in Walford, while Finlay, played by Ashley Byam, later departed the soap too.

‌



Felix went on to become a familiar face behind the bar at The Albert, but his role became less prominent before his eventual departure.

His character also broke new ground for the long-running BBC soap through his drag alter ego, Tara Misu.

Speaking about the role after joining the soap, Matthew said: "I am blessed to have the opportunity to step into the heels of the fierce Tara Misu as part of my role on EastEnders.

Article continues below

"It’s a privilege to represent the LGBTQIA+ community and to showcase the creative art of drag to both viewers at home and the residents of Walford."

Like this story? For more of the latest showbiz news and gossip, follow Mirror Celebs on TikTok, Snapchat, Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, YouTube and Threads.

News.title: Dog found dead inside burning vehicle at McDonald's car park as man arrested
News.content:
Dog found dead inside burning vehicle at McDonald's car park as man arrested

Police are investigating after a dog was found dead inside a vehicle following a fire at a McDonald’s car park in Petersfield.

View 3 Images A dog was found dead inside a burning vehicle in a McDonald’s car park. (Image: Google Maps)

A dog was found dead inside a burning vehicle in a McDonald’s car park, sparking a police investigation.

‌



Emergency services were called to the McDonald’s car park on Winchester Road in Petersfield at around 12.15am on June 22.

‌



When crews arrived, the dog was found dead inside the car.

‌



A 28-year-old man, of no fixed address, was arrested on suspicion of arson, causing unnecessary suffering to an animal, driving otherwise than in accordance with a licence and no insurance.

He has been bailed with conditions until September 22 whilst enquiries continue.

Police are now trying to identify two men who were seen apparently attempting to get into the vehicle in a bid to help the dog.

‌



View 3 Images Police are trying to identify two men who appear to have tried to save the dog. (Image: Hampshire Police)

Hampshire Police has been reviewing CCTV footage from the area and has released images of the pair, who officers believe may be able to assist with the investigation.

Officers are continuing enquiries to establish exactly what happened before and during the blaze.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Police are trying to identify two men who appear to have tried to save the dog. (Image: Hampshire Police)

Police acknowledged that the CCTV images are not particularly clear and urged the two men, or anyone with information which could help the investigation, to come forward.

Anyone with information can contact Hampshire Police on 101, quoting reference 44260294619. Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Unseen Liam Payne photo sparks new theory on tragic last hours in released police files
News.content:
Unseen Liam Payne photo sparks new theory on tragic last hours in released police files

One Direction star, Liam Payne, died in October 2024 after falling from the balcony of his hotel suite in Argentina, leaving his legion of loyal fans heartbroken

View 6 Images Haunting pictures of Liam Payne's tragic last hours have been revealed (Image: America TV)

Haunting pictures of Liam Payne's tragic last hours have emerged in new police files including one that has sparked a new theory about his death.

‌



The One Direction star, 31, left his legion of loyal fans bereft in 2024 when he died after falling 46ft from the third-floor balcony of his hotel suite in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

‌



The singer had travelled to Argentina 16 days prior to the fatal fall while waiting for his US visa renewal. He had spent much of the trip with girlfriend Kate Cassidy and businessman Rogelio “Roger” Nores and was reportedly sober during the first two weeks of his stay before Kate returned to Miami on October 14.

‌



After Kate flew home, Liam checked out of the luxury Park Hyatt after allegedly damaging his room and having an angry confrontation with staff. He then moved to the CasaSur Palermo Hotel, where his life was cut brutally short.

View 6 Images One Direction star, Liam Payne, can be seen pacing in his hotel in Argentina (Image: Argentina Police)

A tragic trove of documents, photographs, sworn statements and official reports gathered by investigators after Liam died in Buenos Aires have now been shared.

‌



Heartbreaking CCTV image shows the dad-of-one, hollow-eyed and drawn, stumbling through the corridors just one hour before he plunged to his death, in evidence shared by The Mail.

The report also reveals his family’s heartache, with a sworn statement from Liam’s father Geoff, who told prosecutors his son ‘went away’ when he was in the grip of his demons saying: "He was not in control with what he did. He was not Liam."

Liam allegedly started calling the front desk of his hotel asking for drugs and was ordering multiple bottles of Johnnie Walker Black label whisky from room service.

‌



View 6 Images The star checked into the CasaSur Hotel where his life was tragically cut short (Image: Argentina Police)

The police files reportedly contain messages from a ‘Reception’ group WhatsApp chat on October 14, where hotel manager Gilda Martin wrote: "This person is going to be very intense throughout his stay. It’s important that we tell him 'no', always kindly and with excuses. This is to stop him from continuing to be aggressive. Or at least not so much."

Reception replied: "Will do whatever we can as long as he doesn’t get violent."

‌



Liam reportedly contacted two escorts while at the hotel after finding one of their profiles online. According to their statements, the singer sent pictures of himself in bed and a video proving his identity after one woman struggled to believe she was communicating with the One Direction star. The women said they arrived at the hotel at around 11.30am, showed identification at reception and were allowed up to his room.

View 6 Images Liam reportedly contacted two escorts while at the hotel after finding one of their profiles online (Image: Argentina Police)

They claimed there was a language barrier because Liam only spoke English while they spoke Spanish, meaning they relied on a translation app to communicate. They said: "During our time there, we had sex with him, which was consensual sex, only once, and he wore protection."

‌



The pair said they spent around two hours with Liam before asking again for the agreed payment. They claimed he instead offered them his Rolex, which they said he later smashed when they refused.

One of the women said: "We told him we only wanted money so he took it and smashed it. He told us he didn’t care about the money.

"And then he broke the TV, he punched it. He made us understand that he could smash everything because he knew he could pay for it."

‌



View 6 Images The escorts claimed they had 'consensual sex; with Liam at his hotel (Image: Argentina Police)

While pictures have previously emerged of a smashed TV set, Liam's Room 310, was said to be ‘carnage’.

Photos show sheets were pulled off the bed, what appeared to be streaks of blood on the bathroom sink, and drug paraphernalia littered the room, including burned Coca-Cola can lids, a blackened spoon and half-burned candles. Police and prosecutors believe Liam heated the powdered cocaine into a liquid ‘crack’ form of the drug which he snorted or injected.

‌



CCTV footage later shows the star pacing back and forth. while the escorts, who had left Liam's room, were in the lobby. The women left around 3.30pm and Liam’s friend Roger arrived at 4pm, the footage shows.

The men talked, but Roger said his Liam did not seem impaired and so he left again. Forty minutes later, the star was dead. Roger was originally charged with ‘abandoning’ Liam, but all charges were dropped.

Initially five individuals were charged in connection with the incident, including allegations of drug supply and negligence. By 2026, three suspects had all charges dropped, including businessman Rogelio Luis “Roger” Nores, who was cleared of manslaughter and drug‑supply accusations

‌



Meanwhile, two remaining defendants, accused of selling cocaine to Payne, are in plea negotiations that may result in shorter sentences.

View 6 Images This image has posed a new theory surrounding Liam's death (Image: Argentina Police)

Exactly what happened to Liam may never been known, however another new image of the star has posed a new theory surrounding his death. In the grainy photo from the police files, the singer is dressed in a green top and grey jeans, swinging around a pole outside the hotel at 3.21am in the early hours of the morning before he died.

Article continues below

A source close to the investigation last week said police consider the pole picture ‘highly significant’ because it showed Liam’s upper body strength. This suggests that, rather than being suicidal, he may have been trying to climb out of his hotel room, confident he could hold his weight, before he lost his grip and died.

Liam lost his life thousands of miles from home, leaving his family, friends and millions of fans heartbroken. He also left his beloved son, Bear, without a father, in a tragedy, which left the world in mourning.

News.title: Andy Burnham to embark on cost of living tour through the UK
News.content:
The prime minister is set to announce "a series of measures to make life easier" for those struggling with the cost of living in the coming days, Downing Street says.

No 10 says Andy Burnham's plans are to "give people some room to breathe". He will also focus on ways of "improving high streets" as he embarks on a tour of the UK.

But the government is facing continued pressure over its early release scheme for prisoners in England and Wales â with criticism of the fact that two of PC Andrew Harper's killers will be eligible from next year.

Burnham is also likely to face pressure for more action on the cost of living â although significant interventions are unlikely before October's Budget.

Even then, Chancellor John Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

The prime minister has been on holiday this week, but Downing Street said he would be in "listening mode" in the coming days as he tours the UK's nations and regions and works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

A spokesman for the prime minister said: "He thinks Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles â like hidden pricing and consumers being ripped off â must be accepted as part of life.

"He doesn't think that's right. That's why he's going to start rolling out a series of pro-consumer cost of living measures to give people some room to breathe."

The spokesman added: "He's also going to be kicking off his summer tour around the country, getting out of Westminster and meeting people where they are.

"The prime minister is going to be in listening mode to help inform his 10-year plan to bring back hope and make Britain better off."

There are, though, likely to be continued questions about the forthcoming early release scheme, due to start in October.

One of Burnham's first acts in Downing Street was to order a review which limited the range of people who would be eligible.

But those convicted of manslaughter will still qualify for the scheme â including two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

The prime minister has faced calls from PC Harper's family, former senior police officers and opposition politicians for them to be denied early release.

But he has said he cannot go any further without risking prison capacity. Downing Street said on Saturday night that position remained unchanged, despite reports the prime minister could revisit the case.

Despite early release schemes having been in place for England and Wales since late 2023 under the previous Conservative government, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has warned the prison population could overtake capacity as soon as this November.

The latest figures for England and Wales, recorded on 23 August, showed the prison population was at 86,495 - more than 97% of useable capacity.

On the cost of living plans, the Conservatives said the government's "tax hikes and red tape are hammering our high streets".

Shadow chancellor Mel Stride said: "This is breathtaking hypocrisy from Burnhamâ¦ they are forcing businesses to close, destroying jobs and driving up prices for the public.

"Meanwhile, Labour are plotting to release dangerous criminals onto our streets, leaving people feeling unsafe in their communities."

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokeswoman Daisy Cooper said struggling high street businesses "need more than a new PM embarking on a vanity tour this summer".

She said the PM should adopt the Lib Dem plan for high streets: "That means reversing the damaging jobs tax, delivering an emergency VAT cut for hospitality, replacing broken business rates and cracking down on the ghost landlords leaving our shop fronts vacant."

Reform UK's economic spokesman Robert Jenrick said: "If Andy Burnham wants to help people with the cost of living, he should scrap the green levies and taxes on energy bills and rule out tax rises at the Budget."

News.title: Killed a month after his wedding - why PC Andrew Harper's story touched so many
News.content:
On the night of 15 August 2019, Lissie Harper got a knock at the door. She thought it was her husband Andrew coming home from work.

Instead, it was uniformed officers, there to tell her that the man she had married four weeks earlier had been killed while on police duty.

"Everything I had known in my life to be true was robbed away. Every ounce of beautiful peace, gone," Lissie later said of the moment she was told.

They had met as teenagers and were together for 13 years.

In her eulogy at his funeral, Lissie recalled how Andrew would pass her notes in class.

They were, she said, "true childhood sweethearts, loving one another more and more with each passing day".

They had been about to go on their honeymoon.

But, on that night nearly seven years ago, everything changed.

The case has been back in the headlines because two of PC Harper's killers â Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole â will become eligible to be released early under government plans to tackle prison overcrowding.

As the disturbing details of the case are revisited, his family, fellow officers and the public are outraged once more â at what happened, and at the perpetrators' impending release.

PC Harper's death was brutal and devastating, causing shock, anger and an outpouring of grief across the country.

Pictures of the smiling faces of his teenage killers laughing and joking as they left court only added to that anger.

PC Harper had been about to head home at the end of a long shift when he and a colleague were called to reports of a burglary.

He was "going beyond the call of duty", the prosecutor at the Old Bailey trial in 2020 said.

During the case, haunting dashcam footage from the police patrol car was played showing the moment PC Harper confronted teenagers Henry Long, Bowers and Cole down a dark country lane. He then disappeared from view.

His ankles had got caught in a strap trailing behind the car being driven by Long that had been used to tow a stolen quad bike.

PC Harper was dragged for over a mile. He died on the road. His police badge and stab vest were found scattered along the route.

The three teenagers were tried for murder. In the end, the jury convicted Bowers and Cole of manslaughter. Long had already pleaded guilty to that offence.

It meant the jury was not sure that PC Harper's killers knew they were dragging the officer behind the car.

But the Judge, Mr Justice Edis, described it as a manslaughter case which was "very close to a case of murder" in its seriousness.

News.title: How weight-loss medication is changing relationships with alcohol
News.content:
There is a growing body of research into the link between weight-loss drugs and alcohol consumption.

The drugs, with brands including Wegovy, Mounjaro and Ozempic, contain semaglutide or tirzepatide, which mimic a natural hormone called GLP-1. This suppresses appetite and keeps people feeling fuller for longer, helping them to lose weight.

Early research suggests that because these drugs affect the reward response in the brain, they can reduce cravings for substances including alcohol and nicotine, says Dr Christian Hendershot of the University of South Carolina.

He published a small-scale study, external in 2025 in which participants with alcohol use disorder craved alcohol less while taking Ozempic. Alcohol use disorder, sometimes referred to as alcoholism, is described by the NHS as drinking in a way that is harmful.

A study, external from the University of Colorado Anschutz published last week also suggested that GLP-1 medications in pill form led to fewer days of heavy drinking in people with mild to moderate alcohol use disorder.

People taking the drugs told BBC News that alcohol had affected them in different ways: some said their cravings for it had gone, drinking had made them feel nauseous or uncomfortably full, or they had got drunk more quickly. Others said they had not noticed any effect on their relationship with alcohol.

Before she started taking Wegovy, Lisa says she drank between six and eight bottles of wine a week with friends. But she had sometimes worried about whether this was too much and whether it could damage her health.

NHS guidance, external is that people should not drink more than 14 units a week on a regular basis, which is about six medium glasses of wine or six pints. Drinking too much in the long term can lead to liver damage, high blood pressure and increased risk of cancer.

Lisa says that since starting on the medication she has more than halved her consumption. At a recent day festival, she drank three glasses of wine over the course of nine hours. Previously, she would have had two bottles plus a couple of vodka mixers, she says.

Alcohol has always been a big part of her social life and when she stopped drinking for a few weeks in the late 2010s, she realised friends had stopped inviting her to social events. It led her to start drinking again.

This time round, Lisa says that she still looks forward to drinking wine, but after having a couple of glasses she simply cannot stomach any more.

"I still feel involved in things because I'm still drinking but drinking a lot less," Lisa says.

For years, Warren Thomas, 45, from Colchester, had enjoyed an occasional beer with his family after work, as well as one or two heavy drinking sessions with his friends each month.

But when he spoke to his friends on weight-loss medication about his plans to start taking Mounjaro, they warned him that it could affect how much he drank.

Warren says he noticed the effect within 24 hours of his first dose in mid-June. "I just don't want to drink," he says. "I've just got no appetite for it."

When he went out for his friend's birthday last month, he felt "light-headed and a little bit giddy" after two beers, he says.

"My tolerance level to drinking is now zero," he says.

There is no formal advice in the British National Formulary, a guide to dispensing medicine used by doctors and pharmacists, about whether people on weight-loss drugs should stop drinking alcohol, says Prof Russell Hearn, a GP and professor of medicine at King's College London.

But he gives careful advice to his patients. "Alcohol has a lot of calories in it and if your goal is to lose weight, drinking less will definitely help you with that alongside changing your diet while you're on a GLP-1," he says.

For people like Lisa and Warren, drinking less alcohol has been a happy bonus. But recent graduate Faye Goodwin, 20, feels that it has hampered her social life.

When Faye drinks she says she gets nauseous very quickly and sometimes throws up or gets bad acid reflux.

Faye, who got in touch with BBC Your Voice, has been taking Mounjaro since she was 18 and does not really know what it is like to drink alcohol without the impact of weight-loss medication. But she says she once took a month off the jabs and was able to drink without experiencing any nausea.

News.title: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
News.content:
After wildfires caused more damage in France this year than at any time since World War Two, many are left asking a single question: Why?

A major driver is that climate is changing as a result of the well-documented way humanity is burning fossil fuels. Temperatures are only rising.

But with records showing that nine out of 10 French wildfires are started by humans, the government in Paris is trying to attribute blame - although it is itself accused of being underprepared for the infernos that have now scorched more than 300,000 acres this summer.

The interior ministry has announced 420 arrests of people alleged to have either started the fires deliberately or by accident. Among them are 166 minors.

In one case, a 23-year-old man has been accused of deliberately starting 10 fires in the space of five days in the south-eastern Var area last month. He faces 15 years in prison and a â¬150,000 (Â£128,000) fine, if convicted.

Many others have been tried and immediately sentenced, such as a man who received a three-year jail sentence for starting three recent fires in the Raon-L'Ãtape forest in the Vosges region.

"Only a few square metres of vegetation went up in smoke," noted L'Est RÃ©publicain, the newspaper that reported the story.

Other prosecutions have been perceived as heavy-handed and unjust. A homeless man and someone with severe autism have reportedly been handed jail terms for throwing cigarette butts.

"I was amazed at the number of arrests, it feels excessive," admits Muriel Gestas, a lawyer who has represented several people accused of arson, including two firefighters. She doubts many will lead to a conviction.

The newspaper Le Monde is also unconvinced. It questions to what extent police have examined these cases, given the short time frame.

The authorities' silence on the details - the specific charges, notably whether they involve intent and how the numbers compare with past seasons - rules out any meaningful comparison with previous years, it argues.

But Bordeaux prosecutor Renaud Gaudeul told Le Monde that a tough approach was justified by current circumstances.

"The conditions for a charge of endangering lives are met for those who throw a cigarette butt or light a barbecue in wooded areas. It only takes a tiny spark for it to start," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

News.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
News.content:
"Eyes peeled," comes the order from the front passenger seat.

Obediently, we scan the ends and tops of logs, looking between low scrub and patches of vivid wildflowers for a flash of stripes or a dart of movement.

Eluding us is the numbat, a rare Australian marsupial which could be the love-child of a chipmunk and an anteater.

Numbats were once populous across the bottom half of the continent, but Dryandra Woodland â in the south-western corner of Australia â is one of the few places they remain.

As we slowly roll along bush tracks, researchers explain how this annual trip helps plot the species' survival.

Classified as endangered until this month, numbats have been bouncing back. This team's efforts have seen them scratched off the international red list of threatened species - a rare glimmer of hope in a country facing an extinction emergency.

This part of Australia is the front line of that crisis: a last stand for many species driven to the brink by feral pests, disease, urban development, habitat destruction and climate change.

Winging over our car at one point is the endangered Carnaby's cockatoo. On an island just off the coast is one of the last surviving pockets of the world's rarest marsupial, the Gilbert's potoroo. Diving in the sapphire waters around it is the increasingly scarce Australian sea lion.

News.title: Zendaya saw me on the red carpet and her jaw dropped - I'm still in shock
News.content:
"I can't zip this! Mummm?"

This was 29-year-old Zainab Jiwa, calling out for help squeezing into a corset while filming a "get-ready-with-me" TikTok video. It's a scene many 20-somethings still living at home will relate to.

The difference is, Zainab was on her way to the recent London premiere of The Odyssey, one of the summer's biggest blockbusters.

She was invited there as a guest and says she caught the eye of Hollywood megastar Zendaya, thanks to her custom look: a striking gold gown complete with a hood.
