"She just walked past, and she saw me there. Her jaw just dropped, so did mine," Zainab tells me.

"It was just a stare-off for a minute, and she was like, 'Oh my god, amazing, amazing,' and then she just walked off."

"Iâm still in shock,â she adds. âThe thought of her noticing my outfit blew my mind."

The interaction went viral, external with 19m TikTok views. Her phone blew up.

While Zendaya has been ruling the red carpets with high-fashion "method dressing" â where stars match outfits to a film's themes â Zainab is perhaps proving that independent creators like her can give Hollywood a run for its money.

Zainab, who is Muslim and wears a hijab, is also often one of the only people covering her hair at premieres, but she says finding ways to incorporate modest wear is part of the fun.

"Even though you're covered, you can still find a way to be on theme.â

News.title: Why eclipse chasers are crossing continents for solar spectacle: 'It's like the World Cup'
News.content:
On Wednesday, parts of Europe will be plunged into daytime darkness as the moon passes in front of the sun, temporarily blocking its light and casting a shadow across the continent.

For many of us, it will be a once-in-a-lifetime experience. But for some, following eclipses has become something of an addiction.

Armed with two high-spec cameras, a specialist telescope and a drone, Mark Griffiths has spent two days driving from Cheshire to Galicia - one of the best places to view the eclipse - to record the event.

It's a hobby that started six years ago, when he went to Shetland to see the northern lights - though the weather was so dreary he "didn't see anything".

But it didn't put him off and he soon found he couldn't stop. He loved the thrill of witnessing and capturing the sky's most spectacular events.

News.title: What is clearing and what do I need to know ahead of results day?
News.content:
At first, he wanted to take a gap year after his A-levels so did not apply for university, but was persuaded to go by family and friends after achieving "great grades".

On the day, with the help of his A-level teachers, he filled in a Ucas form, applied to six universities via clearing and picked the University of Manchester to study politics and modern history.

"The good thing about clearing is that you can apply to as many universities as you want, unlike with Ucas, where you are limited to five," he says.

"That was definitely stress-relieving," he says.

For those on the fence about university, Nasir recommends people put in a Ucas application "just in case" to avoid the stress of results day.

That's a piece of advice that is echoed by Wade.

"You will need a referee, which is why I'd suggest doing it now," she says.

"Let's say [you've] got to email the teacher, the teacher's got to add a reference, then Ucas only gets sent once all of those parts are sent together."

Nasir says he wished he was more prepared for clearing, and advises students to write down some notes on location, accommodation and cost for each university you contact.

"Make sure you know whether you qualify before calling," he says.

"With my university I was required to have a specific A-level, so make sure you meet the requirements."

News.title: More areas of UK likely to move into drought as fifth heatwave builds
News.content:
Sunday will be a warmer day across many areas with temperatures widely getting up to the mid to high twenties Celsius. South-east England will be even hotter where temperatures could rise as high as 33C.

As of 12:00 BST on Sunday, a few locations in the south-east had already surpassed 30C, setting a new record for the UK's highest number of 30C days in a calendar year. The previous record was 34 days in 1995.

After a cooler day on Monday, temperatures will then rise widely across the UK from Tuesday.

In Scotland and Northern Ireland, temperatures will typically reach the low to mid twenties.

In England and Wales, temperatures will rise into the mid to high twenties Celsius and widely across east Wales, central, eastern and southern England in excess of 30C.

The heat is set to peak on Thursday, with readings of 35C possible in south-east England.

If this happens, it will be the fourth consecutive month of 35C or more being recorded.

The threshold for declaring an official heatwave is likely to be reached widely across England and Wales, making it the fifth heatwave of the year for many.

Yellow heat health alerts are in effect for most of England until 21:00 BST on Tuesday, warning of impacts for health and social care services and an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

These are likely to be updated in the coming days as heatwave conditions develop.

News.title: Family 'devastated' as hit-and-run driver who killed boy, 13, to have early prison release
News.content:
The family of a 13-year-old boy killed in a hit-and-run say they are "devastated" after being told the driver who caused his death has had his sentence reduced.

Kaylan Hippsley died three days after being struck by a car driven by Harley Whiteman on Brecon Road in Hirwaun, Rhondda Cynon Taf, on 29 February 2024.

Whiteman was originally sentenced to six years and nine months in prison and banned from driving for eight years and four months but, after Kaylan's family appealed, High Court judges increased the sentence to nine years.

Now, the family has been told Whiteman can be released under licence as early as this autumn as part of the UK government's Sentencing Act early release scheme.

News.title: Kellie Bright to leave EastEnders after 13 years
News.content:
EastEnders star Kellie Bright is to leave the soap after playing one of its key characters, Linda Carter, for 13 years.

She arrived in Albert Square with on-screen husband Mick, portrayed by Danny Dyer, when they became the new owners of the Queen Vic pub.

Carter's matriarch character has been central to major storylines including plots about murder, sexual assault and alcoholism.

Bright said she made the "tough decision" to leave more than a year ago but "happily" agreed to stay on to be part of an "exciting storyline".

The BBC has promised "unmissable drama" before her on-screen exit, which is said to be a "while away" yet.

Executive producer Ben Wadey described the actor as being "the beating heart of EastEnders" and said she had become "a classic EastEnders icon".

Viewers have seen the much-loved character at the heart of many emotional storylines including in 2014 when she was raped by her brother-in-law Dean Wicks.

More than 7m people watched the episode which prompted dozens of complaints. The sexual assualt led to long-running story arc about family conflict and trauma.

News.title: Banksy works cost public almost £150,000
News.content:
Three artworks by street artist Banksy have cost taxpayers almost Â£150,000 in cleaning operations and security so far, with the bill expected to rise.

The largest single cost relates to a mural painted on the Royal Courts of Justice in September 2025, where removal efforts and security have so far cost more than Â£85,000.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) says it has spent Â£50,000 trying to remove paint from the wall of the Grade II-listed building in Carey Street. A further Â£35,300 was spent on overtime and security costs.

The spending was disclosed to the BBC through Freedom of Information requests and is likely to reignite debate over whether Banksy's work is vandalism or valuable public art.

News.title: Rare turtle to be sent back home in 5,000-mile 'incredibly emotional' trip
News.content:
It has taken almost two years to plan, including building a special temperature-controlled crate for him, and co-ordinating complex paperwork across two countries.

Rhossi normally lives in the sea, but has to travel out of the water â first by helicopter from Anglesey to London, then by cargo flight to Houston, Texas, USA.

It means the journey needs to be completed as quickly as possible, and staff have to be constantly on hand to make sure he does not dry out or dehydrate.

Davidson said: "We have to make sure that the shell is really well lubricated, so we spread Vaseline all over to stop it drying out and flaking off.

"The same for the skin â it's really delicate â and especially the eyes, which both have to be lubricated before he goes into the crate and again just before takeoff, or he will start to peel like someone getting sunburned.

"But I have had to go to the checkout in a chemist's with about eight tubes of KY Jelly and three tubs of Vaseline and explain what's happening when I get strange looks."

News.title: Stray cats showing up at raves, gigs and pubs now have own merchandise
News.content:
Celebs pulling in punters with a club appearance is nothing new. But did they ever have so much fur?

At venues in Coventry at least, the glitterati wear whiskers these days.

It began when two stray cats made city venues their home, becoming social media stars thanks to the incongruous sights of tail and turntable, pint and paw.

While one shows up at gigs and rave nights, the other is a bit more pub than dub. But each now has his own range of merch... and visitors flock for a glimpse of these meeow-vers and shakers.

Murphy was first spotted living beneath a bush before wandering into the car park of The Old Windmill pub in the city centre, "rake thin" and in need of care.

Now a permanent resident, he has become a firm favourite with customers.

"We've had people who've never been in the pub before, but have seen him on social media," said the venue's Peter Dunkley. "They come in and the first question is 'where's Murphy'?"

Across town, Fargo is a well-known figure at Fargo Village, the creative hub after which he is named.

Regularly spotted around the site's shops and bars, he too has become an attraction in his own right, mixing among ravers and drinkers.

Fargo Village staff have set up an Instagram account in an effort to track down his owner, and it has attracted a loyal following of fans eager to keep up with his daily adventures.

News.title: Week-long celebration of Irish music and culture to come to a close
News.content:
From buskers on the bodhran to musicians firing up their fiddles, the atmosphere and the celebration of music and culture has been joyful.

Lots of people have been making the most of the open sessions, with chances to showcase their hidden talents, or learn new skills.

Visitors to the festival have been immersed in live music sessions, interactive workshops, dance classes and pop-up pubs for the past seven days.

These include artists such as Ãirdan, Seoid, Celtic Roots and many more.

The closing ceremony will begin at 18:00 BST, kicking off with a performance from singer-songwriter and harpist Niamh Noade, and it will close at midnight with a performance from the winners of the Senior CÃ©ilÃ­ Band Competition.

More information can be found here., external

Aside from the performances at City Hall there will be a range of activities across the city centre.

The Seamus Heaney centre at Queen's University Belfast is hosting an exhibition, called Something to Say that looks at the personal and professional friendship between Seamus Heaney and David Hammond.

You can visit an Irish language craft and culture market at Conway Mill and there will be plenty of sessions, external going on with workshops and arts activities available.

News.title: Charity watchdog investigates aid charity over alleged Hamas links
News.content:
A UK-based aid charity is being investigated by counter-terror police and the charity watchdog over alleged links to Hamas.

The Charity Commission launched an inquiry into Muslim faith-based charity Al-Khair Foundation on Friday.

Counter Terror Policing London (CTP) also confirmed investigations into the charity, with two search warrants on addresses in Croydon, South London.

The foundation said it is "co-operating fully" with the inquiry and had filed a serious incident report with the watchdog before it was launched.

A spokesperson for the foundation said: "Everywhere we work we are firmly committed to ensuring that the funds entrusted to us by our generous donors are used for their intended purpose: meeting the humanitarian needs of poor and marginalised people in the communities we serve.

"Al-Khair Foundation is deeply committed to supporting those in need in Gaza. Our significant support over many years has included providing food parcels, hot meals, clean water, medical aid, shelter materials, winter assistance and orphan and family support."

The Al-Khair Foundation provides emergency relief and developmental support in "some of the world's most impoverished areas", according to its website.

Hamas is designated as a terrorist organisation by the UK and US governments.

It comes after last week Mohammad Yousef Hasna, 45, from Istanbul, Turkey, was arrested in the UK over US accusations of conspiring to funnel money and supplies to Hamas through a "sham charity".

The US Department of Justice did not name the "sham charity" in their press release.

The Al-Khair foundation maintains that Hasna is not an employee but works with one of its global partners to enable the delivery of aid around the world.

Hasna is being held following his arrest by the UK's National Crime Agency (NCA) and pending extradition proceedings before he can be taken to New York to face the US charges.

The US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York alleged Hasna used his senior role at a "purported global humanitarian organisation to coordinate directly with Hamas's senior leadership regarding the delivery of funds and supplies to Gaza, and the distribution of those funds and supplies at Hamas leadership's instructions".

Hasna is charged with conspiring to provide material support to Hamas, conspiring to finance terrorism and financing terrorism.

Each charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, the US Department of Justice said.

US Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg said: "The money that flows from sham charities like the one described in the complaint fuels Hamas's terrorist activities, including the atrocities the group committed on October 7".

The Charity Commission said the Al-Khair Foundation recorded an income of more than Â£74m in the financial year ending 31 July 2025. The commission added it was made aware of the allegations against Hasna and "immediately started examining the serious concerns raised".

"The commission has now escalated its engagement to a statutory inquiry," the commission added.

Al-Khair is also subject to a legal order restricting some financial transactions being made without the consent of the Charity Commission.

News.title: Fearne Cotton lived like a ‘hermit’ when she was ‘crippled by anxiety’
News.content:

Fearne Cotton has revealed how she became a “sort of hermit” during a difficult period that left her “crippled with anxiety” and “debilitated”.

The TV and radio presenter, 44, underwent surgery in December 2024 to remove two benign tumours from her jaw, and shortly after announced that she had split up with her husband Jesse Wood, who is the son of Rolling Stones star Ronnie Wood, after 10 years of marriage.

The couple are parents to son Rex, 13, and daughter Honey, 10.

The former Top of the Pops presenter, who is now the host of the Happy Place podcast, told The Sun that she felt overwhelmed by “a snowball of anxiety” during this tough time.

“I was very scared of getting things wrong, like getting socialising wrong,” she told the paper.

“I built up a snowball of ­anxiety that could be triggered by just stumbling over a word in a conversation.”

open image in gallery Cotton said she struggled to work and drive while dealing with debilitating anxiety ( Getty Images )

“I could go to a party and then come home and repeat every word that I’d said on a loop, and I couldn’t sleep.”

She added that she “had panic attacks constantly”, and her anxiety meant that she “couldn’t drive a car, couldn’t do a lot of TV work I’d been doing”, leaving her feeling “­debilitated”.

The presenter, who started her career as a host on CITV at the age of just 15, said that learning to adopt a less rigid approach to wellness, as well as learning “how to channel anger in a healthy way”, had helped her.

open image in gallery Cotton said she’d concluded that worrying too much about wellness is ‘bonkers’ ( Getty Images )

“If it’s debilitating to the point where you can’t do things, you’ve got to face things that you might not want to face,” she said.

Cotton admitted she was “having no fun” while she was focusing on wellness, and realised “if I go out and have fun, and I have a couple of drinks, yeah, I might feel a little ropey the next day. But worrying too much about this stuff is bonkers”.

She has recently returned to TV after several years away from the screen, co-hosting Landscape Artist of the Year, which will air on Sky Arts in 2027.

“I was really petrified about stepping back into that ­environment,” she admitted. “But more recently, I felt good enough to push myself out of my comfort zone and back into TV.”

“Before, I’d get so worked up, and go, ‘Am I doing a good enough job on TV? Will people like this?’”

News.title: Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund LIVE: Emirates Cup team news as Odegaard and Gabriel start pre-season friendly

Why Arsenal Want Bruno Guimaraes So Badly

Arsenal bid to step up their pre-season preparations as the Premier League champions take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

News.title: Kosovo’s acting prime minister pelted with eggs by opposition
News.content:
Kosovo’s acting prime minister Albin Kurti was pelted with eggs during a parliamentary session in Pristina on Saturday, as the government moved to constitute its new parliament following the June 7 snap election.

The attack, led by an opposition lawmaker, came after Kurti asked the speaker for additional time to negotiate a political agreement with opposition parties, a request which was granted.

Vetevendosje, the election-winning party, convened Saturday’s session despite objections from opposition parties and some constitutional law experts, who argued it was unconstitutional.

They argue that the 30-day deadline set by the Constitutional Court for constituting parliament expired on Friday.

News.title: Irish ‘gangland crime boss’ Daniel Kinahan extradited from Dubai: ‘I’m looking forward to getting back home’
News.content:

Suspected Irish crime gang boss Daniel Kinahan has been handed over to authorities from his home country after being extradited from Dubai.

Kinahan, who was ‌arrested in ‌Dubai in April, was named ⁠as one of three leaders of the Kinahan organised crime group by the United ‌States in ​2022 when ‌it ⁠offered a $5m ⁠reward for their ‌arrest.

He was also identified in the High Court in Dublin as a senior figure who “controlled and managed” the operations of the organised crime group.

His extradition, reported by United Arab Emerites state media on Sunday, comes after several months of preparations, in what is said to be one of the biggest security operations the Irish government has ever launched, following the arrest of the Dublin boxing promoter in April.

Reacting to news of his planned extradition, Kinahan said that he was “looking forward to getting back home”.

Kinahan, aged in his late 40s, was detained on foot after an arrest warrant was issued by the Irish courts in relation to alleged serious organised crime, including drug and firearms offences.

An Irish government jet took off from Casement aerodrome in Baldonnel on the outskirts of Dublin on Saturday morning.

According to The Times, it has now taken off from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and is due to arrive in Ireland this evening.

Snipers on roofs, bomb-proof vans for transportation, decoy vans and signal jammers in prison ceilings will be deployed to bring Kinahan to trial,The Times reports,

Kinahan spoke about the process on Saturday, leaving a voice message that was shared on Instagram by podcaster James English, in which he said that he was “looking forward to getting back home”.

He said: “The security is going to be crazy. I am sitting here reflecting a little.

“Then I’m thinking of what happened, how I got here, all the stuff that’s happened in my life, the whole lot, just reflecting. It’s like bittersweet. It’s going to be nice to get back.

“I was always proud to be Irish.I wanted to do good things and big things but obviously life didn’t go that way for me with all the stuff and all the media, what people think of me you know and the perception they have of me, but I am still so proud to be from Ireland.

“I’m looking forward to getting back home.”

In 2016, an attempt was made on Kinahan’s life at a boxing weigh-in at the Regency Hotel in Dublin.

After that, he left Ireland, first to go to the Costa Del Sol in Spain and later settling in Dubai for the past decade.

The Kinahan cartel was involved in a feud with the rival Hutch crime gang in Ireland, which began in 2015 and resulted in 18 deaths.

Typhoon Dolphin made landfall on China’s eastern coast on Sunday, bringing torrential rain and strong winds and triggering warnings of flooding and landslides.

The typhoon has already swept through Japan's southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

Typhoon Dolphin made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province at about 5.30pm (0930 GMT) on Sunday, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 42 metres per second (151 kmph) near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the ⁠Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

Torrential rain is forecast through August 10 across Zhejiang, Shanghai, northern Fujian, northeastern Jiangxi, central and southern Anhui, and ⁠much of Jiangsu. Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250-500 mm (9.8-19.7 inches) of rain, according to forecasters.

After landfall, Dolphin is forecast to track westward before slowing over central and southwestern China and gradually losing strength, Wang Haiping, chief forecaster at the National Meteorological Centre, told state broadcaster CCTV.

That could prolong heavy rain and raise the risk of flooding and landslides, especially in mountainous areas and along smaller rivers.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country and more than 1 million people were evacuated from their homes.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

In addition to evacuating at least 30,300 people, Shanghai has cancelled about 1,500 flights, according to flight-tracking data provider VariFlight.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong, surnamed Chen, said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled because of Typhoon Dolphin.

He said ⁠the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

“To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life,” Chen said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level III, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level III emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal ​passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects halted and 290 construction vessels moved to ‌sheltered waters.

The water resources ministry said the Qiantang, Yong, Jiao and Shuiyang rivers could see major flooding, while smaller rivers in the hardest-hit areas could rise above warning levels.

Authorities warned of a high risk of geological disasters in parts of Zhejiang, while residents in areas covered by a red mountain-torrent warning were told to follow local evacuation orders.

Shanghai's Yangshan port cleared ​ships from its berths and moved more than 500 small ‌and medium-sized vessels to shelter ahead of Dolphin, the city's ​maritime safety administration said. Scientists say global warming has made extreme weather more likely, including stronger typhoons.

The father of the deceased shooting suspect in Thailand’s Debsirin Nonthaburi school issued an apology on Sunday to the victims and their families affected by the teen’s deadly rampage.

A 14-year-old boy opened fire at his school on Friday, killing six people on the premises before turning the gun on himself.

Hours earlier, he had allegedly shot dead his grandparents at home before coming to the school in Nonthaburi province, just outside Bangkok, police officials said.

At least 14 people remain hospitalised, of whom seven remain in critical condition Saturday, said Thailand’s health ministry. It said most of those wounded were between 12 and 14 years old.

More than 20 ‌people were injured ​in Thailand's worst mass shooting since ‌2022, which has reignited debate over firearms ​control in Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation.

The deceased shooter’s father emerged from the Plai Bang police station on Sunday morning after being questioned by the investigators.

He was seen swarmed by a crowd of journalists and camerapersons on his way to the car.

Mourners pray for 12-year-old school shooting victim Naphat Chaima at Wat Lat Pla Duk in Nonthaburi province ( AFP/Getty )

He issued his first remarks since the incident and apologised in Thai. “I’m sorry,” he said, reported ABC News.

“I am deeply sorry to all the families,” he said in a brief statement.

Authorities have continued their investigations into the rampage as police officials on Sunday said the boy had used social media to learn how to use a firearm and watched violent content online.

In a similar incident, police said, the 14-year-old had an air gun confiscated by a teacher last year.

"According to witness interviews, the perpetrator had begun showing interest in studying the use of firearms for some time, about one to two years," said Atthapol Anusit, deputy commissioner of the Provincial Police Region.

The official said police so far had interviewed 17 witnesses. A knife had also been found in the boy’s bag and other evidence found at the crime scenes included a firearm, spent cartridge cases and a personal computer.

"After examining the PC, it was found that the child had watched social media content involving violence," the deputy commissioner said, but added there was no evidence yet that he had practiced shooting.

Mr Atthapol said that last year a teacher had confiscated a BB gun, a type of air gun, that the boy took to school.

The boy had lived with his grandparents for 12 years after his parents had separated, he said.

Authorities in Thailand are now facing a major challenge of tightening access and control of guns among its population.

The ministry of education said it would develop ‌new safety protocols over the next three months, including mental ​health screenings and a system to refer at-risk people ‌to specialists, drills for emergency response ⁠plans, a drive to stamp out bullying and better detection to ⁠stop items from being taken into schools.

The UK economy is expected to have recorded another quarter of growth as businesses find ways to cope with the fallout of the Iran war, but some industries are coming under increasing pressure, economists think.

Figures from the Office for National Statistics being published on Thursday are set to show a degree of resilience in the economy in the face of supply chain issues and price pressures linked to the conflict, as well as a period of political uncertainty.

Some economists think gross domestic product (GDP) will have increased 0.4% for the second quarter, between April and June.

This would mean the economy has continued growing after a 0.6% rise in GDP for the first three months of 2026.

Rob Wood, chief UK economist for Pantheon Macroeconomics, said this would show “the big picture is that the economy has remained resilient to the hit from the war in Iran”.

open image in gallery

It comes as the services sector – the most dominant in the UK economy – strengthened in May, largely coming from professional services and scientific research and development.

Furthermore, recent data has pointed to factories and manufacturing firms stockpiling in anticipation of supply shortages and price rises, which has helped keep growth elevated.

But a weaker picture may be emerging from June as the heatwaves bring mixed results for businesses and some industries come under increasing pressure, economists said.

Mr Wood is expecting monthly GDP to dip by 0.1% in June, “reversing the 0.1% gain in May, as a sharp fall in construction activity drags on growth, while services and industrial production stagnate”.

open image in gallery England reaching the World Cup semi-finals is expected to have helped boost spending in July (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Thomas Pugh, chief economist for RSM UK, said he was expecting the services industry to have been dragged down by a fall in hospitality activity, despite the Fifa World Cup kicking off in June.

Mr Pugh said its own business surveys suggest “consumers were likely switching away from restaurants towards pubs to watch the World Cup, rather than increasing the total amount of spending”.

But he added: “There could still be a boost to activity in July, given the scorching weather and England reaching the semi-finals.”

Mr Pugh has a slightly more positive outlook for June, forecasting monthly GDP to have risen by 0.1%.

“All told, we expect GDP to nudge up in June, helped by a big jump in erratic mining activity,” he said.

“That will be enough to deliver 0.4% growth for Q2 (the second quarter), as strong momentum from Q1 (the first quarter) and consumers smoothing through higher inflation helped to support solid growth.”

A quarterly increase in GDP will likely be good news for new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who has said he wants to achieve “growth in every postcode” of the UK.

He opened a new headquarters for the centre of Government in Manchester in late July, named No 10 North, where he is expected to work once each week as part of his move to push power out of Westminster.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

Sports.title: Andrey Santos claims he can replace Casemiro at Man Utd after £50m transfer from Chelsea
Sports.content:
ANDREY SANTOS insists he can be the solution to Manchester United’s defensive midfield problem and replace compatriot Casemiro.

United bought Santos, 22, from Chelsea in a £50million deal after missing out on Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes.



Santos was billed by United director of football Jason Wilcox as a box-to-box midfielder last month but the Brazilian has occupied a deeper role in United’s pre-season friendlies.

United want to sign a third midfielder to offset the departure of Casemiro and long-term injury to Manuel Ugarte, and recently made a fresh enquiry about Aurelien Tchouameni at Real Madrid.



But Santos has offered to fill the void left by Casemiro, who was released in June.

He said: “So my qualities, I like and prefer playing more deep like a number six.”



“So I try to help my teammates without the ball and with the ball. I love breaking the lines.

“Casemiro, for me he’s like a legend. So now he’s gone from United and now I’m here. So I feel that I can do like Casemiro did in the last season and I’m here to do it.”

Santos has started in all four of United’s friendlies and is set to make his full competitive debut in their opening Premier League fixture against Hull City on August 22.

Chelsea loaned out Santos four times in three-and-a-half years to Vasco da Gama, Nottingham Forest and Strasbourg before cashing in.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Eyebrows were raised at the initial £48m United paid Chelsea for Santos, who failed to make Brazil’s 26-man World Cup squad.

Santos’ longest starting run at Chelsea was six games under Liam Rosenior, who also managed him at Strasbourg.

With Santos now primed for a regular starting role at United, he acknowledged he faces a step up from his time as a squad player at Stamford Bridge.

He said: “My first week is a little bit funny because you know when you change, so it’s a new club.

“But since my first day I feel at home, so I think this is so important for me and for new players as well.



“Is it a step up from Chelsea? Yeah, of course. I know Chelsea is a big club as well, so I think thank you for everything Chelsea did for me in my period.

“But now Chelsea is gone, here is my home right now. And I want to be here for a long, long time and win so many trophies.

“I have my goals and I hope that I can work with my teammates with my goals and and hope to win some trophies.”

Sports.title: Man Utd are trying to do what Sir Alex Ferguson did with Michael Carrick in midfield
Sports.content:
A WEEK after Andrey Santos claimed he couldn’t speak, he spoke enthusiastically about his start to life at Manchester United.

Nobody at United had pinned down a specific role for Santos. It was to his credit that he billed himself as “like a number six”.



United director of football Jason Wilcox promised that Santos has “the ability to impact the game at both ends of the pitch”.

Michael Carrick has spoken vaguely about the most expensive signing of his brief tenure.



The caginess from United is predictable amid their wish to sign a third midfielder. But they are making no promises and Santos offers them a get-out.

Mason Mount’s foot injury that forced him off in the 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain is not serious. A well-placed source said Mount is fine and he looked it as he smiled and walked freely towards the team coach in Gothenburg.

Youri Tielemans showed some class on his cameo and Kobbie Mainoo is now back. So that is four options in midfield.

Yet United are lacking a statement signing there. Manchester City bought Elliot Anderson, Tottenham blew competitors out of the water for Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes has bolstered Arsenal.

Chelsea already have Moises Caicedo. United clearly lack an enforcer and Santos is not a physically imposing presence.

Santos, 22, has been tidy in possession and it is a pity he was not pitted against PSG’s Portuguese pair Vitinha and Joao Neves from the start in Sweden.



Mainoo’s breakthrough at United was on his maiden pre-season three years ago when he held his own against Arsenal’s Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard in New Jersey.

Mainoo’s good fortune was that his tour debut fell in a year between the World Cup and the European Championship.

Anderson, Rice and Caicedo were all wanted by United and all slipped the net.

United took Manuel Ugarte off PSG’s hands the summer they recruited Neves.

United have not bought a genuine game-changer in midfield since Sir Alex Ferguson’s heyday, and Ferguson developed such a midfield blind spot that he did not sign one in his final four years in charge.



There is an argument that the last midfielder who fit that game-changing billing was Carrick 20 years ago. Owen Hargreaves and Anderson both joined in 2007 and United won the Premier League and Champions League, yet the pair’s impacts were short-term.

Already, there is evidence that Carrick the coach is trying to replicate what he experienced as a player during his 12 years at United.

In 2006, Ferguson reinvented United’s midfield to offset the departure of Roy Keane. Carrick, an £18.6million signing from Tottenham, received Keane’s squad number and there the similarities ended.

Paul Scholes, sidelined for five months with an eye problem, returned in a deep-lying role.

Scholes’ vision was no longer impaired and his partnership with Carrick led to a first Premier League title in four years.



After Scholes came out of retirement in January 2012, he and Carrick started together 15 times in the second half of that campaign and United lost only twice.

Their collapse from an eight-point advantage at the Premier League summit with six games to play was sparked by Ferguson resting Scholes for a midweek 1-0 defeat at Wigan Athletic. Scholes then lined up in the remaining five games.

Whenever a midfield crisis brewed, Ferguson tended to turn to Scholes and Carrick. Overall, they started alongside each other 113 times.



It was not a foolproof partnership. Barcelona ran rings around United in two Champions League finals that Scholes did not start in.

Those occasions confirmed Carrick never attained the world-class status that Xavi, Andres Iniesta and Sergio Busquets did.

Mainoo, Santos, Tielemans and Mount are all technical-based players. Certainly not in the class of Scholes and Carrick in their pomp but there are parallels with what Carrick is trying to rekindle.

Santos and Mount have started in all four of United’s friendlies, out of necessity. Tielemans is on the scene now and may partner Santos against Leeds United in Dublin on Wednesday if Mount is not risked.

United started to display glimpses of transitioning to a more controlling style at the tail-end of last season and that is long overdue. It was beyond Erik ten Hag, who lamented that United would “never” replicate the style of his Ajax side.



The only tactic United remain synonymous with is the counter-attack and they have to get away from that.

Carrick’s approach goes against the grain of the beefed-up Premier League. The £116m and £75m fees forked out for Anderson and Guimaraes suggest there is little sign of teams becoming lightweight.

Santos failed to make the cut for the Brazil World Cup squad and his £50m fee, still steep, indicates he is lower down the food chain.



He also faces the added pressure of coming up against players United had lined up before they turned to him.

Santos will not have to wait long. The first Manchester derby of the season is on September 13 at Old Trafford, where Anderson can expect an inhospitable reception after dubbing City as the “kings of Manchester”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Santos was so softly-spoken at the Ullevi Stadium that it was difficult to hear him as United’s kit men hauled equipment down a nearby ramp.

He will have to turn up the volume against Anderson.

Sports.title: Footie star, 29, suffers terrifying injury as he falls down tunnel celebrating goal – then finds it has been disallowed
Sports.content:
STAR PLUMMETS Footie star, 29, suffers terrifying injury as he falls down tunnel celebrating goal – then finds it has been disallowed

BRAZILIAN fans watched on in shock as Coritiba star Jacy plummeted down a tunnel while celebrating a disallowed goal.

The 29-year-old hopped over the advertising hoardings but disappeared down a chute built into the playing surface, which leads to the away dressing room.



There was a terrifying moment when Jacy cleared the barriers and realised he had nowhere to go but downwards.

The tunnel is normally covered, but it was opened by ground staff as half-time approached.



Team-mates raced over to check on Jacy, who reappeared moments later before stumbling to the ground.

Medics came over to treat the defender as he took a minute to collect himself behind the goal.

To add insult to injury, the goal he was celebrating, which he thought had put Coritiba 2-0 up, was chalked off by VAR for offside.

Jacy was able to play on for the rest of the half but came off early in the second when it was clear that the fall had taken its toll.



Coritiba ended up beating Brazilian top-flight opponents Chapecoense 2-1 on Saturday night thanks to goals from Tiago Coser and Pedro Rocha Neves.

Strangely enough, this is not the first time the tunnel at Estadio Couto Pereira has caused havoc.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

In 2014, centre-forward Joel also came a cropper during Coritiba’s clash with Sao Paulo.

And he was helped up by the same security guard who was on the scene when Jacy took a tumble this weekend.

Sports.title: Torquay footballer, 18, diagnosed with brain tumour as club sends love and support after two operations
Sports.content:
'NOT ALONE' Torquay footballer, 18, diagnosed with brain tumour as club sends love and support after two operations

AN 18-YEAR-OLD Torquay footballer has been diagnosed with a brain tumour.

The women’s team of the Devon club posted the sad news about young player of the season Roxy Thomas on Instagram on Friday.



Torquay confirmed Thomas – who joined the club a year ago after progressing at Plymouth to make her first-team debut aged 16 – has had two surgeries this week.

And they shared a classy message to show their support for the left-back, a key member of Ryan Perks’ side that went unbeaten to win the South West Regional Women’s Football League Premier Division title and earn promotion back to the FA Women’s National League.



Torquay United Women also won the Devon Women’s Premier Cup and League Cup in an emphatic treble.

They shared a photo of Thomas in action and said: “Everyone at Torquay United is sending their love and support to Women’s Team player Roxy Thomas and her family following her diagnosis with a brain tumour.



“Roxy, 18, has undergone two operations over the past few days as she begins her treatment, and everyone associated with the Club is thinking of her during what is an incredibly difficult time for Roxy and those closest to her.

“Her teammates have been rallying around Roxy and her family since receiving the news, while the Club will provide whatever support it can during the weeks and months ahead.

“The Club will also be supporting a JustGiving appeal to help Roxy and her family with the costs associated with her treatment and care.

“Further details, including how members of the Yellow Army can contribute, will be shared in due course.



“We know the Torquay United community will want to show Roxy just how much support there is for her.

“For now, everyone at Plainmoor sends Roxy and her family our love, strength and very best wishes.

“We’re all with you, Roxy.”



Torquay players held up her No3 shirt at Saturday’s National League South match against Horsham in a sign of support.

And plenty of Torquay fans and followers flooded the comments section of the post with best wishes to Thomas.

One said: “Thinking of you, Roxy.”

Another wrote: “Best wishes to Roxy, hell of a player knows how to win a battle.”

A third typed: “Sending our best wishes to Roxy and her family.”



And a final user replied: “You got this Roxy.”

And Torquay United Women Chairman Rob Hawes added: “Roxy is a very special young woman and has made a huge impression on everyone at the Club in such a short space of time.

“The news has understandably affected everyone connected with the women’s team deeply.

“Our focus now is simply on supporting Roxy and her family in whatever way we can.

“They should know that they are not facing this alone.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Roxy is one of our own and the entire Torquay United family – players, staff and supporters – is right behind her.”

Sports.title: Georgina Rodriguez poses in tracksuit bottoms as confused fans line streets for Cristiano Ronaldo wedding that never was
Sports.content:
GEORGINA RODRIGUEZ had fans in a spin when she posted a social media video of her relaxing in tracksuit bottoms instead of sporting a wedding dress.

The Argentine model, 32, and Cristiano Ronaldo were expected to tie the knot at Funchal’s cathedral before heading to a glitzy reception at the £1,100-per-night Savoy Palace hotel.



It was thought that the loved-up couple were preparing to get hitched on the Al-Nassr forward’s home island of Madeira yesterday.

But there were no wedding bells for Rodriguez and Ronaldo – leaving their followers confused.



Fans had lined the streets outside Funchal’s cathedral in hope of getting a glimpse of their idols.

And Rodriguez followers were frustrated when a different pair of newlyweds were seen coming out of the venue.



Instead of gearing up for the biggest day of her life, the social media personality chilled out in a pair of tracksuit bottoms.

Rodriguez, who was filmed doing a workout at the gym earlier this week, uploaded a short video onto Instagram Stories showing her enjoying a relaxing day.

She also tagged the outfit’s brand in the unexpected upload after striking a pose.

It has led to question marks over when Rodriguez and Ronaldo, 41, will get married.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Manchester United legend was spotted wearing a diamond ring less than two weeks ago.

And that sparked speculation they would become husband and wife in the coming days.

But they have kept their fans guessing after they were a no-show at Funchal’s cathedral.

Ronaldo’s dreams of lifting the World Cup were crushed when Portugal were knocked out by eventual winners Spain last month.



And the five-time Ballon d’Or winner is now gearing up for a new Saudi Pro League season with Al-Nassr.

He is working under former Tottenham and Nottingham Forest chief Ange Postecoglou, who was appointed as the Riyadh-based side’s boss ahead of the new campaign.

ELEONORA INCARDONA treated fans to a string of stunning snaps as she gears up for the new season.

The Italian presenter, 35, is preparing to front DAZN’s coverage of Serie A this term.

Sports.title: Alexia Putellas ready to be ‘pushed to the limit’ in debut WSL season after stunning London City Lionesses free transfer
Sports.content:
ALEXIA PUTELLAS is prepared to be pushed to the limit in her debut WSL campaign.

The 32-year-old completed a stunning free transfer to London City Lionesses last month after ending her trophy-laden 14-year stay with Barcelona.



Now she is gearing up for a completely new challenge in what she considers to be one of the most competitive leagues in the world.

Putellas said: “You never know which will be the result of the game, so it’s a very competitive league week after week.



“We haven’t started [the season] yet but if I have to imagine all the games will push you to your limit. It’s a very entertaining league. That’s a key point for the fans.”

Having swapped Barcelona for Bromley, the two-time Ballon d’Or winner is now eager to develop further as a player – despite having already won 40 major trophies.



She continued: “It will be different for sure but that’s why I’m here, because I’m looking forward to improving as a footballer, as a person as well.

“It’s being more of a complete player as much as I can, so learning new things, playing with and against other players, just trying to find where my limits are.

“It will take time because, of course, it’s a new beginning, a big change for me but I’m so excited to be here.”

Putellas had extensive conversations with London City owner Michele Kang prior to making the move and was particularly impressed by the ambition of the club.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

London City Lionesses were only promoted to the WSL last year, but Kang has plans to develop them into a European powerhouse.

Putellas added: “The first conversation was about what the club wants and how ambitious the project is. I want to be part of that journey, bring the experience I have and learn as a player and make me more complete.

“I made the move for that and just being in another position that I’ve never been in and in my opinion this league can give me that.

“Always, day after day, I want to learn things. I’m learning new things and that’s the way I see this job. Just keep going, never be stopped and be as better as I can.”



As well as speaking to Kang, Putellas also got in contact with former Barcelona team-mates Keira Walsh and Lucy Bronze – both now at Chelsea – who briefed her on life in England.

“Some of them told me that it’s a hard league and they’re gonna kick me,” she laughed. “No, just joking!

“But no problem, I’m ready for that or I’m trying to be ready. Just enjoy the league because the games are crazy and even if you go for an away game it’s like something’s different, something special and I’m ready for enjoying all of that and being ready for what the games will be for me.”

Putellas could make her debut on the opening day of the season when London City Lionesses host Manchester United on September 4 at the Copperjax Community Stadium.

Sports.title: Thorslund ends Johnson's undisputed run to become world champion again
Sports.content:
Dina Thorslund is a world champion again after ending Cherneka Johnson's undisputed run to cap an emotional return to the sport.

Just over a year after vacating her WBC and WBO bantamweight titles because she was pregnant, the undefeated Thorslund fought aggressively from the start to snatch the WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida.

Thorslund (25-0, nine KOs) vacated her titles in June 2025, and a month later she announced on social media that she had suffered a miscarriage.

She returned to the ring in January and defeated Almudena Alvarez to capture the vacant WBC interim featherweight title. Then Thorslund, who is 32 years old and from Denmark, dropped back to bantamweight to fight for the undisputed championship.

Sports.title: McKenna vows middleweight domination as heir to Golovkin and Canelo
Sports.content:
New world champion Aaron McKenna is just getting started.

He secured the IBF middleweight title with a victory over Etinosa Oliha on memorable night at the 3Arena in Dublin.

Now he wants to take on the mantle of Canelo Alvarez and Gennadiy Golovkin by dominating the middleweight division.

He is targeting other champions. Denzel Bentley holds the WBO title, Carlos Adames the WBC and Erislandy Lara the WBA. McKenna is calling for all the top 160-pounders to fight one another.

"It doesn't matter [who's next], whoever wants it. I'm easy to find now, I have a belt. There's no hiding any more. I want to collect every single belt in boxing. I'm the best middleweight and super-middleweight in the world. I don't mind jumping up," he told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive the heart-warming moment that saw Stevie McKenna watch his brother Aaron win the IBF world middleweight title

"I've been thinking about this moment since I was six years old. It just goes to show, don't give up, always stay true to yourself. You can do anything."

His ambitions extend far. "The middleweight division's there to be took over. It's been dying for years since GGG (Golovkin) and Canelo left it. I said it again, a year ago, I think I'm going to be the man to take it over," McKenna declared at his post-fight press conference.

"No one really believed me. Until you put in performances like that and then they start listening. In life you've got to prove yourself sometimes. Tonight I've done that. I just hope one of the other world champions will take on the fight so we can clean up this mess of a division."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aaron McKenna's IBF middleweight world title fight against Etinosa Oliha

He promises he will not shy away from any challenge.

"Anyone. I've said it before and I'll say it again I will literally fight anyone out there. I just want to unify, whatever it takes, prove I'm the best in the world. That's the sport of boxing. You look back in the day, the 80s and 90s, they all fought each other," McKenna said.

"And this is exactly why Zuffa Boxing's going to be the future. It's already taking over. Everybody's fighting each other, there's no more hiding."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna had an incredible entrance ahead of his fight with Oliha, first coming into Sinead O'Connor's The Foggy Dew and then Faithless' Insomnia!

For the time being, he can enjoy his accomplishment.

"Twenty-one years in the making," he concluded. "I don't know how long this is going to take for this to seep in that this has finally happened that I've become world champion. I've been dreaming of this.

"For it to happen now, honestly it's literally unbelievable. I can't describe it."

Sports.content:
True Love heads the markets for the 2026 renewal of the Prix Maurice de Gheest - live on Sky Sports Racing at 3.40pm.

3.40 Deauville - True Love headlines strong field in Prix Maurice de Gheest

Today's feature on Sky Sports Racing takes us to Deauville, where True Love headlines the Group One Prix Maurice de Gheest.

The 1000 Guineas winner was narrowly touched off at the track in last month's Prix Jean Prat over a mile, with Jersey Stakes winner Thesecretadversary taking out the honours that day. Having won the Cheveley Park Stakes over this distance in September, she clearly has sufficient speed for this test and her versatility will be invaluable in her future career as a broodmare. Wayne Lordan makes the trip to France for the ride, replacing Ryan Moore in the plate.

Stolen Kiss has rapidly improved this year since being dropped back into sprinting trips. The clear improvement also has seen this colt beat last year's winner, Sajir, on back-to-back occasions as well as finishing a very close fourth in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes. That is probably the best piece of form in the race and although he has to give weight to True Love, he could put it up to her under Alexis Pouchin.

Fresh from a successful Goodwood Festival, Wathnan Racing will be keen to strike again - this time with William Haggas' Division. This son of Kingman has hit the crossbar a few times this year, finishing second in the Sandy Lane Stakes and then third in the Commonwealth Cup - beaten both times by Venetian Sun. He was a commendable fifth in the July Cup and could easily pop up and win this.

Samangan isn't dismissed but will have to show more after being beaten last time out by Division and True Love in successive starts, albeit by narrow margins. Take Charge Star represents Johnny Murtagh and enters calculations, having only been beaten by True Love's conqueror Thesecretadversary by a neck in the aforementioned Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot.

3.05 Deauville - 2000 Guineas third Distant Storm returns

Distant Storm returns to the track after not being seen since May in the Group Three Prix Daphnis.

Charlie Appleby is bang in form and sends this son of Night Of Thunder to France in search of a first win since September. In the meantime, he was third in a Dewhurst and began this campaign with a third place finish in the 2000 Guineas. The form of the race has worked out well with fifth place Thesecretadversary taking out the Jersey Stakes and Venetian Prince winning the Italian Derby. The mount of Billy Loughnane today closed the gap on Gstaad in the Irish 2000 Guineas and could progress further in the Godolphin blue.

Komorebi was second in the French 2000 Guineas but subsequently disappointed when stepping up in trip for the Prix du Jockey Club, where he finished 10th. Dropping back to the mile looks to be the way to go and if he repeats his performance when last seen over that distance, he's a big contender.

Campacite was beaten one place into 11th by Komorebi in the French Derby after also chasing him home in April. However, the form with Hawk Mountain on his penultimate start is interesting and a repeat of that would make him a player.

Lord Clover lacked the turn of foot to mount a meaningful challenge in the German 2000 Guineas the last day, but on his prior French form could trouble the judge.

5.01 Chepstow - Crimson Road bids to follow up course and distance success

Crimson Road rounds off the card on Sunday afternoon at Chepstow, looking to follow up the win over course and distance here last month in the Capital Windscreens Supports Chepstow Centenary Celebrations Handicap.

On his fourth start for John and Rhys Flint, he skipped clear inside the final furlong and has been raised 3lb for that success but could easily go in again here.

Pride Of Nepal disappointed last time out at Epsom but was bang in form prior, winning four in a row - including a course and distance success here in June which completed the hat-trick. Carrying top weight today, this Tony Carroll gelding will surely put it up to Crimson Road.
