Poland’s top administrative court has upheld a decision by the finance ministry to withhold state subsidies from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party due to campaign finance irregularities. The decision was welcomed by the government, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying that there will be “no money for grifters”. PiS, however, argues that the money is being withheld for political reasons and accuses the authorities of “Russian standards”. Naczelny Sąd Administracyjny oddalił w środę kasacje ws. dotacji i subwencji dla PiS. – Miażdżący dla PiS wyrok podtrzymany! – stwierdził szef MF Andrzej Domański https://t.co/bcL18WbiYf — OKO.press (@oko_press) August 6, 2026 The dispute dates back to August 2024, when the National Electoral Commission (PKW) rejected PiS’s financial report for the previous year’s parliamentary election campaign after identifying around 3.6 million zloty (€838,000) in unauthorised expenditure. As a result, the PKW ordered that PiS should lose 10.8 million zloty from the state subsidies that political parties in Poland receive based on their level of electoral support. The party would normally have received 25.9 million zloty based on its 2023 election result. The decision triggered months of legal wrangling, with PiS arguing that the funding should be restored after the Supreme Court upheld its complaint against the PKW’s decision. However, finance minister Andrzej Domański refused to release the money, saying there were unresolved legal doubts over the ruling. The finance minister has refused to comply with the electoral commission's decision to pay out subsidies to the opposition PiS party He says there are "legal doubts" over the issue. But PiS says he is obliged to pay and will be held criminally responsible https://t.co/ZwIZRqn5tp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 9, 2025 Those doubts stem from a broader dispute over the controversial and contested judicial reforms implemented by PiS when it ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. The chamber of the Supreme Court that ruled in PiS’s favour was created as part of those reforms. It has previously been found to not be a legitimate body by both the European Court of Justice and European Court of Human Rights because it contains improperly appointed judges. After the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling, the PKW initially said it would not recognise the decision until the chamber’s legal status was clarified. Two weeks later, however, it reversed that decision and approved PiS’s financial report. Domański still declined to restore the subsidy, arguing that the PKW’s resolution was internally contradictory. While it approved the payments, it also stated that the chamber’s ruling should come from a body recognised as a court and that it was not determining whether the chamber met that standard. PiS challenged Domański’s decision. However, its case was initially rejected by a lower court in June last year, and that decision has now been upheld by the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), which is the final court of appeal for administrative issues. The NSA found the minister had acted lawfully in withholding the funding. It also said the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling had no legal effect because it had been issued by a body that was not a properly constituted court, reports news website OKO.press. The ruling was welcomed by Domański, who called it a “crushing blow to PiS” and said that “yet another PiS lie has been exposed”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk, meanwhile, wrote on social media: “Just as we said, there is and will be no money for grifters.” Tak jak mówiliśmy, dla przekręciarzy pieniędzy nie ma i nie będzie. https://t.co/4Kqexj6NoC — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 5, 2026 The PKW’s decision to cut PiS’s funds was made after it found that government resources – including from the justice ministry, Government Legislation Centre (RCL) and Research and Academic Computer Network (NASK) – had been used to support the party’s election campaign. However, PiS has always argued that the decision was a political one, implemented at the behest of the new Tusk government in order to undermine the main opposition party. Radosław Fogiel, a senior PiS lawmaker and former party spokesman, said that the new NSA ruling “does not change the essence of the matter: it unlawfully deprives the main opposition party of the subsidy to which it is entitled. World.title: Polish prosecutors end 10-year treason investigation into Tusk over Smolensk air disaster
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! After a ten-year-long investigation, prosecutors have concluded that Poland’s government in 2010 – which was led by current Prime Minister Donald Tusk – was not guilty of “diplomatic treason” in its response to the plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party – which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 and is led by Lech’s twin brother, Jarosław – has always rejected the findings of official Polish and Russian investigations into the crash, which found it to have been an accident. Instead, PiS claims that the disaster, which claimed the lives of 96 people, many of them senior Polish state officials, was caused deliberately by Russia and then covered up with the help of Tusk’s government. However, while PiS launched various investigations during its time in power, it has never substantiated its claims. And prosecutors now say that there is no evidence that diplomatic treason, a crime that carries a potential prison sentence of up to ten years, took place. Uprzednio wygrałem sprawę cywilną z posłem @OficjalnyJK, który w efekcie musiał wpłacić 50,000zł na siły zbrojne broniącej się Ukrainy. Teraz potwierdzenie @PK_GOV_PL: nie było żadnej zdrady dyplomatycznej ani żadnej intencji jej popełnienia. Oczywiście żaden z kłamców… https://t.co/VKZHlF5xkX — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) August 5, 2026 Wednesday’s announcement by the National Prosecutor’s Office was welcomed by Radosław Sikorski, the current foreign minister, who held the same role in 2010. He condemned the “Smolensk liars”, such as Jarosław Kaczyński, who he suggested had exploited the tragedy for their own benefit. “They brainwashed millions of people, divided families, stirred up hatred within the nation,” he wrote. “They’ll burn in hell for it. But the power, money and satisfaction they gained from spitting on their rivals – that’s theirs.” The idea that Smolensk was an assassination of Lech Kaczyński has been a core part of PiS rhetoric. In 2022, for example, Jarosław Kaczyński said that the decision was made “at the highest level of the Kremlin” and Tusk’s government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”. Smolensk was an “attack decided at the highest level of the Kremlin”, says Jarosław Kaczyński ahead of the 12th anniversary of the crash. Donald Tusk's government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”, he adds https://t.co/5ae0gHJj3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 4, 2022 The investigation into diplomatic treason – a crime consisting of acting to the detriment of Poland while authorised to represent the country in relations with foreign states or organisations – was launched in August 2016, less than a year after PiS had come to power. Among the individuals who had formally notified prosecutors of a potential crime was PiS deputy leader Antoni Macierewicz, who from 2015 to 2018 served as defence minister. He has been the foremost proponent of conspiracy theories around the Smolensk air disaster. In their notifications to prosecutors, Macierewicz and the others accused Tusk and other officials of, in their relations with Russia, deliberately choosing a legal basis for an investigation into the crash that was unfavourable to Poland by giving it no real influence over how it was run. However, prosecutors now say that, after ten years in which they questioned 488 witnesses, gathered extensive documentation and requested legal assistance from several countries, they have “concluded that no crime of diplomatic treason was committed”. In a statement explaining the decision, the National Prosecutor’s Office said that the legal basis chosen for cooperating with Russia on an investigation – Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation – was, in fact, “the most advantageous solution” for Poland. It ensured the participation of Polish representatives in the Russian-led investigation, including access to the wreckage and crash site. Other legal options would have offered no greater benefits and involved significant risks, concluded the Polish prosecutors. They acknowledged that Russia “subsequently failed to fulfil some of its obligations arising from the adopted procedure”, but said this should have no bearing on assessing the decisions that were previously made on setting up the investigation. The defence ministry will notify prosecutors of 41 suspected crimes linked to a commission established by the former PiS government to investigate the 2010 plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński https://t.co/aEAlmk9lDM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 24, 2024 The prosecutors also found that, not only did Polish officials choose the best legal solution, but there was also “no evidence indicating that individuals authorised to act on behalf of Poland, including the prime minister and members of the Council of Ministers, acted with the intent to harm Poland”. Given that the crime of diplomatic treason requires intent, this finding further reinforced the decision to drop the investigation. However, the prosecutors note that their decision can still be appealed. At the time of writing, neither Kaczyński, Macierewicz, nor other senior PiS figures had commented on the prosecutors’ announcement. However, it is likely they will point to the fact that the current national prosecutor was appointed by Tusk’s government after it had removed the previous PiS-era incumbent in a legally questionable move. The Supreme Court has issued a ruling that effectively found that the government unlawfully replaced a senior prosecutor earlier this year However, the justice minister says the ruling has no legal force as it was issued by illegitimately appointed judges https://t.co/9fCE6d18uy — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 27, 2024 In 2020, in a separate civil case, a court ordered Jarosław Kaczyński to apologise for accusing Sikorski of “diplomatic treason” in relation to the Smolensk crash. Two years later, after Kaczyński had refused to comply with the ruling and Sikorski published the apology himself, Kaczyński was ordered to pay the costs. In 2024, an investigation by Tusk’s government found that the PiS administration had wasted tens of millions of zloty on a commission, headed by Macierewicz, that was tasked with re-investigating the Smolensk disaster. It notified prosecutors of dozens of suspected crimes relating to the functioning of the commission. Macierewicz, however, accused the government of spreading “lies and disinformation” designed to “protect Putin”. Jarosław Kaczyński has been ordered to pay 700,000 zl (€150,000) to publish an apology to ex-foreign minister @sikorskiradek. World.title: Where to See the Partial Solar Eclipse in Prague and Across Czechia
World.content:
Skywatchers in the Czech Republic will have two reasons to look up on the night of August 12.

A partial solar eclipse will be visible in the evening, followed by favorable conditions for watching the annual Perseid meteor shower.

The eclipse will be visible across Czechia shortly before sunset, with the Sun low over the western and northwestern horizon. In Prague, the partial eclipse is expected to begin at about 7:19 p.m., reach its maximum at 8:12 p.m. and end around 8:27 p.m.



At the height of the eclipse, the Moon will cover about 86 percent of the Sun’s disk in Prague, making the event particularly noticeable if skies are clear.

The eclipse will look different depending on where observers are located. The farther east they are, the later the eclipse will begin and the less of it will be visible. In eastern Czechia and much of Slovakia, the maximum phase will take place after sunset, when the Sun is already below the horizon.

The event will be a partial eclipse in Central Europe, while a total solar eclipse will be visible in parts of Greenland, Iceland and Spain. Astronomers and eclipse enthusiasts are expected to travel to those areas to experience totality.

A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, blocking part or all of the Sun from view. In Czechia, the eclipse will be especially low on the horizon, so observers will need an unobstructed view toward the west and northwest.

Several Czech observatories are preparing public observing events. A list of locations and other information about the eclipse is available through the Czech astronomical website astro.cz.

Perseid meteor shower will follow

The same night will also offer good conditions for watching the Perseids, one of the most prominent annual meteor showers.

The shower will reach its peak during the early hours of August 13, when the Moon will be only a few hours past its new-moon phase. With virtually no moonlight in the sky, faint meteors should be easier to spot.

The Perseids are active from July 17 through August 24, but the best opportunity this year will come during the night of August 12-13.

Under dark skies and favorable weather, observers away from cities could see between 50 and 80 meteors per hour.

Light pollution will be the main obstacle for anyone hoping to see large numbers of meteors. The best locations are well away from major cities, ideally several dozen kilometers from strong sources of artificial light.

World.title: Non-Alcoholic Beer Sales Rise by More Than 25% in Czechia
World.content:
Beer remains a staple of the Czech shopping basket, but new sales data from online supermarket Rohlík shows that drinking habits are gradually changing.

Traditional lagers still dominate, while non-alcoholic beer is recording the fastest growth among the main beer categories.

The category has grown by more than a quarter over the past year, with Birell among the brands driving the increase. Birell sales alone are up by almost 20%.



Together with flavoured beers and radlers, non-alcoholic beer now accounts for close to one-third of all beer sales on Rohlík.

Beer from small and regional breweries is also gaining ground, with sales increasing by more than 11%.

The biggest decline is being recorded among craft beers grouped by style, including IPA and APA. This is currently the only major beer segment experiencing a year-on-year drop.

Czech brands continue to dominate the market. More than nine out of every 10 beers sold through Rohlík are from domestic brands.

Imported beers, however, are growing at a faster rate. Their sales have increased by 18% year-on-year.

Beer sales peak at the weekend

Friday is the busiest day for beer sales, with roughly twice as much beer sold as on Monday. Friday and Saturday together account for almost two-fifths of the category’s weekly sales.

Orders containing beer also tend to include significantly more items than orders without beer, suggesting that customers often buy it as part of a larger meal or weekend shop rather than as a standalone purchase.

Seasonal patterns have also shifted. Beer sales during this year’s summer months have reached levels comparable with the December Christmas peak.

World.title: Prague 7 Plans Floating Swimming Pool on the Vltava in Holešovice
World.content:
A floating swimming pool could be built along the Vltava River in Prague’s Holešovice district, near U Vody Park.

Prague 7 City Hall is considering using a section of the waterfront near the Port 7 development for the project.

The municipality hopes the pool could be ready within three years, although the cost has not yet been determined.

The project is still in its early stages. The district is currently looking into whether it could obtain older or unused pontoons and adapt them to create the swimming facility.



One of the main questions is where the pool water would come from. Prague 7 is considering both the Vltava and the municipal water supply.

The aim would be to use this data to determine when swimming in the river is considered safe. Čižinský has suggested introducing a simple traffic-light system similar to those used in cities such as Copenhagen and Amsterdam, allowing swimmers to see whether conditions are suitable.

According to Čižinský, the Vltava generally has good enough water quality for swimming, although conditions can deteriorate after heavy rainfall.

Recent measurements support this concern. Prague hygiene officials have been monitoring the water at Branická beach since the beginning of this year. The water has generally received a rating of two on the five-level scale used by hygienists.

The Holešovice proposal is not the first plan to introduce a floating swimming facility on the Vltava.

A similar idea was included in an earlier proposal to transform Prague’s riverfront. The project near Vyšehrad envisaged a large floating structure measuring 69 by 7.5 meters, with a swimming pool and a smaller paddling pool. A second connected vessel would have provided facilities for visitors.

The proposal was later put aside. In 2025, Prague property councilor Adam Zábranský of the Pirates said the investment was not among the city’s priorities.

World.title: Construction Disrupts Prague Tourists and Businesses During Peak Summer Season
World.content:
Construction projects across Prague’s historic center are proving a pain for tourists and locals alike who say the clumps of dirt, building supplies and equipment block popular sites and make it difficult to move around one of Europe’s most visited cities.



Heading down Národní to the Charles Bridge or going for a beer near the Vltava river now looks more like a vast construction site where tourists need to look out for more than the cobble-stone streets and baroque spires.

“It’s their first time here too, [they’ve] never seen it and now it’s torn up,” said Sherryl, a tourist visiting from the United States with her friends.

A major source of the disruption are upgrades to the public transport system. The central tram route delivering travelers to the heart of the city near the Národní Divadlo stop has been shuttered for weeks.

The disruption has taken a heavy toll on surrounding businesses like Aggeo, an Italian grocery store along the corridor. Its manager, Irena Kumpová, noted a sharp drop in foot traffic from travelers and regular local customers, who stroll by the National Theater on their way to gaze at the artist David Černý’s famous Kafka head.

“I’d rather stay closed… it’s a catastrophe,” remarked Kumpová.

With tourism growing every year in Prague, the widespread construction is making its mark this summer. So far this year, 1.7 million people have visited Prague, marking the strongest start in 15 years, according to Prague City Tourism and the Czech Statistical Office.

Tram services are suspended through the city center, clogging the streets and forcing many to find another way to work or home. For businesses that rely on heavy foot traffic during the busiest months of the year, that means less earnings.

“I have a table outside, but mainly just to signal to people that we’re open, but no one sits there right now,” said Kumpová.

The reconstruction is part of Prague’s broader effort to modernize its transport network, including long-term investments such as the future tram connection to Wenceslas Square and the expansion of Metro Line D as the city seeks to expand public transport.

Not everybody minds the disruption. The loud machines, dusty air, and obstructed sidewalks offer a certain charm for some who view the construction as part of the sightseeing experience.

“Despite the construction, it’s still beautiful,” said Raluca Costachescu, a traveler from Romania.

Written by: Mae Bryant, Bilyana Spasova, Milica Petrušová, Zuzana Kormančíková, Zhanna Bekiryan

World.title: Live Nation and PPF to Run Three Major Prague Venues
World.content:
Live Nation and PPF Group are forming a joint venture that will operate three of Prague’s major event venues — O2 Arena, O2 Universum and Forum Karlín.

The companies plan to invest in the venues and upgrade their facilities, with Live Nation set to hold a 51 percent stake in the new company.

The agreement will bring together one of the world’s largest live entertainment companies and PPF, the investment group that owns O2 Arena and O2 Universum through its subsidiary Bestsport.



PPF has also operated Forum Karlín, which has been owned by Patria Investment Company since last year.

The companies announced the planned partnership in a joint statement. Financial details of the transaction and the amount of the planned investment have not been disclosed. The deal remains subject to the required regulatory approvals.

Under the agreement, the new operator will be responsible for the day-to-day running of all three venues, including event planning and programming. The venues themselves will remain under their existing ownership structures, and their names will not change.

The partners said they intend to invest substantially in the facilities over the coming years. The aim is to improve conditions for audiences and performers while expanding the number of events held in Prague and strengthening the city’s position on the international concert and entertainment circuit.

PPF said the cooperation with Live Nation is also part of its strategy of developing the long-term value of its assets alongside major international companies.

Live Nation Entertainment operates across several areas of the live entertainment industry, including concert promotion, ticketing and sponsorship. Its businesses include Live Nation Concerts, Ticketmaster and Live Nation Sponsorship.

PPF Group is an international investment company with holdings across Europe, North America and Asia. Its portfolio includes telecommunications, media, financial services, real estate, e-commerce, industry and biotechnology.

World.title: Prague to Restore Tram Service Between Holešovice and City Center
World.content:
Residents of Prague 7 will regain a tram connection between Holešovice and the city center from September, with tram line 5 set to operate through the district and continue toward Wenceslas Square.

The change follows months of pressure from Prague 7 officials and local residents, who have called for better tram connections since the cancellation of line 14.

The district had previously requested either the return of line 14 or the introduction of an equivalent service and organized a petition supporting the demand.



The new arrangement will initially be temporary. According to the Prague Integrated Transport (PID) system, two trams will operate on the route at least through December 2026.

Line 5 to replace temporary route

The new service is linked to planned transport changes in Žižkov. Because of a traffic closure there, tram line 34 will be replaced by line 5 in Holešovice.

At Holešovice train station, line 5 will connect with line 6, effectively creating a continuous service between the two routes. Trams will run from the station through the Holešovice area, past the market and across Vltavská Street before continuing toward Wenceslas Square and other parts of central Prague.

For passengers in Holešovice, the move restores a connection that was lost when line 14 was discontinued.

Service could change again next year

The situation between January and June 2027 has not yet been fully settled. According to PID, the final arrangement will depend in part on discussions between the incoming leaderships of Prague 3 and Prague 7.

Maintaining the additional tram service in Holešovice during that period could require limited reductions elsewhere in Prague 3. Another option would be to temporarily return to the existing arrangement using combined tram lines 6 and 34.

PID has warned that permanently combining lines 5 and 6 could also create delays at both ends of the route. Such a change could affect passengers travelling through Prague 2 and Prague 5, even though it would provide the direct connection sought by Prague 7.

World.title: “Ivan, Go Home!” Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
World.content:
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.

The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.

The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.



The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.

The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.

Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.

Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.

The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.

The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

World.title: World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
World.content:
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.

Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.

The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.



The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.

Charlie Plummer leads the cast

American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.

The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.

At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.

One of Norway’s largest film projects

The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.

According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.

Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.

The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

World.title: Viktor Orbán filmed in Serbia with MOL executive and controversial Hatvanpuszta estate architect
World.content:
Former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán was spotted at a popular trumpet festival in Serbia, where he was filmed walking through the streets alongside two figures with close links to Hungarian business and the controversial Hatvanpuszta estate.

Former Hungarian prime minister photographed at Guča festival with two prominent associates

Orbán’s appearance at the Guča Trumpet Festival in the Dragačevo region was reported by Serbian news agency RINA, which published footage showing the former prime minister mingling with festival-goers and posing for photographs.

According to RINA, the former prime minister appeared to be in good spirits and was walking without bodyguards while enjoying the festival in the company of friends. However, the identities of the two men walking alongside him have attracted particular attention.

MOL executive and businessman among Orbán’s companions

One of the men accompanying Orbán was identified as Oszkár Világi, a Slovak-Hungarian billionaire and deputy chief executive officer of Hungarian oil and gas company MOL. Világi is the former head of Slovnaft, the Slovak refinery owned by MOL, and is also the majority owner of Slovak football club FK DAC 1904, based in Dunajská Streda.

Investigative journalist Szabolcs Panyi also identified Világi in the footage, noting his longstanding relationship with Orbán. The two have maintained close ties for years, according to Panyi’s account. Világi’s appearance alongside Orbán is notable in part because the two remained connected despite Hungary’s recent political changes, according to the reporting.

Hatvanpuszta architect also seen in the footage

The other man walking with Orbán was identified as architect Dániel Taraczky. Taraczky has been associated with the development of the Orbán family’s Hatvanpuszta estate, a property that has attracted considerable political and public attention in Hungary.

According to official documents cited in the Hungarian reports, Taraczky acted as an architect representing Orbán’s father, Győző Orbán, during heritage-protection proceedings concerning the estate. He has also reportedly won public procurement contracts connected to a number of construction projects financed with public funds.

The Hatvanpuszta luxury estate. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

Disciplinary proceedings over Hatvanpuszta building

Taraczky’s role at Hatvanpuszta has previously drawn criticism from independent MP Ákos Hadházy. Hadházy filed a complaint with the Hungarian Chamber of Architects over the demolition of a protected 19th-century agricultural building at the estate.

In May 2026, the chamber’s ethics and disciplinary committee ruled at first instance that Taraczky had breached legal requirements and professional ethical rules. The committee suspended his chamber membership for one year and imposed a fine of HUF 800,000 (appr. EUR 2,190), as well as ordering him to pay procedural costs. The ruling was a first-instance disciplinary decision, according to the reports.

A relaxed appearance at one of Serbia’s best-known festivals

The footage from Guča presents an informal picture of Orbán, who is shown walking among festival-goers and stopping to take photographs with members of the public. The Guča Trumpet Festival is one of Serbia’s best-known traditional music events, attracting large crowds to the small town in western Serbia each year.

While Orbán’s presence at the festival itself was relatively informal, the appearance of Világi and Taraczky alongside him has drawn attention to the former prime minister’s relationships with prominent business figures and people connected to projects associated with his family.

World.title: Hungary set to launch EUR 5.5 billion railway upgrade as development plan gets green light
World.content:
Hungary’s ambitious Baross Gábor Railway Development Plan can now move into its implementation phase after the government’s review of the Integrated Transport Development Operational Programme (IKOP Plus) was published in the Hungarian Gazette (Magyar Közlöny).

According to Dávid Vitézy, the development plan will make more than HUF 2,000 billion (approximately EUR 5.5 billion) in railway and other rail-based transport investment available to projects across the country.

The former transport state secretary and current transport and investment minister announced the development on Facebook, saying the publication of the government decision means that projects funded largely through EU resources can officially get under way.

Hungary’s Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy at a railway crossing. Photo: Facebook/Vitézy Dávid

HUF 3,550 billion railway development programme

The Baross Gábor Railway Development Plan is designed to renew Hungary’s rail and other fixed-track transport infrastructure over the next ten years, with a total budget of HUF 3,550 billion.

One of its main sources of funding is the EU-backed IKOP Plus programme. According to Vitézy, HUF 1,406 billion is available for transport developments during the current EU funding cycle, while a further HUF 950 billion has now been committed for projects in the next funding period.

This means that more than HUF 2,000 billion in railway development projects can now move towards actual implementation, he said. Vitézy also highlighted the role of negotiations with Brussels, claiming that Hungary had secured EUR 16.4 billion in EU development funding.

Major railway projects planned across Hungary

The programme covers a wide range of projects, from suburban railways around Budapest to major railway lines and stations across the country.

Among the planned developments are upgrades to the Budapest–Veresegyház–Vác and Budapest–Lajosmizse–Kecskemét railway lines, as well as the modernisation of Budapest’s HÉV suburban railway network.

Preparatory work is also set to begin on the reconstruction of Debrecen’s main railway station, while the Debrecen–Nyíregyháza railway line will be upgraded. The main railway lines towards Miskolc and Szeged are planned to be developed for speeds of up to 160 km/h, while preparations will begin for the reconstruction of the main line towards Pécs.

New intermodal transport hubs are also planned, alongside the modernisation of numerous regional railway lines and stations. The programme could also pave the way for the extension of Metro Line 3 in Budapest and further development of the city’s interconnected tram network on both the Pest and Buda sides.

Read more about the development plan on Daily News Hungary: Hungary unveils EUR 10 billion railway modernisation: New trains, airport rail link and faster journeys promised!

New trains and HÉV vehicles also planned

The Baross Gábor Plan is not limited to infrastructure. It also includes the procurement of new InterCity trains and HÉV vehicles, station renovations, railway track reconstruction and the elimination of speed restrictions caused by poor track conditions.

New battery-powered multiple units are also planned for some non-electrified regional railway lines connecting larger county capitals. Vitézy cited potential services towards Salgótarján and Szekszárd as examples. The plan also aims to strengthen international railway connections and improve rail transport in Budapest, its metropolitan area and major regional cities.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Railway projects can now officially begin

Vitézy described the Baross Gábor Railway Development Plan as a nationwide programme, covering areas from the Budapest metropolitan region and the Great Plain to western Hungary. The publication of the IKOP Plus review in the Hungarian Gazette means that the projects are no longer merely plans on paper: their implementation can now officially begin.

Vitézy said the developments could put Hungary’s rail and fixed-track transport system back on a development path after years of decline.

World.title: Did Russian Mere’s only Hungarian store suddenly close? Questions surround the discount chain’s future
World.content:
The only Hungarian shop linked to Russian ultra-discount retailer Mere has unexpectedly closed, which left customers and observers uncertain about the future of the controversial chain’s Hungarian operation.

According to Világgazdaság, the store, which opened under the name Basket Plus in Budapest’s 18th district in December 2025, is currently listed as temporarily closed. However, it remains unclear whether the closure is merely a technical interruption or marks the end of the retailer’s brief Hungarian venture.

The company operating the shop has not yet provided a public explanation. Attempts to contact the store and its operator, TS Retail Kft., have so far been unsuccessful.

Basket Plus disappears from the Hungarian market – at least for now

The Russian-backed Mere chain had attracted considerable attention before entering Hungary, with the ultra-discount retailer occasionally described as a potential challenger to established chains such as Lidl and Aldi. Its Hungarian operation ultimately opened under the name Basket Plus, after initially appearing under the slightly different name “Basket Plus”.

The shop on Besence Street in Budapest was reportedly still operating just days before its unexpected closure. Google currently lists the store as “temporarily closed”, while there has been no publicly available indication of an official decision ordering the closure.

The shop’s social media activity has also stopped. Its profile had previously been updated almost daily, generally with product promotions, but there have been no new posts since 1 August.

A store of the Russian MERE discount chain. Photo: mere.ws

The sudden closure has prompted speculation among customers on social media. Some commenters claim that the shop is preparing to reopen, while others suggest that employees have already been dismissed and that the closure could therefore be permanent. None of these claims has been independently confirmed.

There are also suggestions online that operational or product-related issues may have contributed to the closure. However, there is currently no publicly available official information supporting such claims. What is known is that the Basket Plus shop opened in December 2025 and was originally expected to be followed by further expansion in Hungary.

Read our article about the store before its opening: Russian discount chain coming to Hungary under new name: here’s when and where it will open

The company behind the shop posted a substantial loss

The financial results of TS Retail Kft., the company operating the shop, provide another interesting piece of the puzzle. According to Világgazdaság’s report, the company’s 2025 accounts have recently become available. They show that its revenue increased from zero in the previous financial year to HUF 202.2 million in 2025, suggesting that it had begun substantial commercial activity.

However, this revenue was far from enough to cover its costs. TS Retail recorded an after-tax loss of HUF 301.7 million in 2025, compared with a loss of HUF 187.3 million a year earlier. Its loss therefore increased by around 61% in one year.

Two major categories of expenditure stand out. Material expenses increased from HUF 18.8 million to HUF 213.3 million, while personnel expenses rose from HUF 166.1 million to HUF 279 million – an increase of around 68%.

The discount chain in Serbia. Photo: depositphotos.com

Notably, personnel costs alone exceeded the company’s entire annual sales revenue by roughly HUF 77 million. Combined, material and personnel expenses amounted to almost HUF 492.3 million, compared with sales revenue of HUF 202.2 million.

Depreciation also increased, from HUF 1.3 million to HUF 3.8 million, while other expenses rose from HUF 20,000 to HUF 652,000. Financial expenses increased significantly as well, reaching HUF 7.4 million. The company employed an average of 26 people in 2025, compared with 18 the previous year, which partly explains the rise in personnel costs.

Overall, TS Retail posted an operating loss of HUF 294.6 million. After financial items, the company ended the year with an after-tax loss of HUF 301.7 million.

Read our article published on the opening day of the Hungarian store: Hungary’s first Mere discount store opens today – if you’re looking for rock-bottom prices, this will be your shop!

Is Mere’s Hungarian expansion in trouble?

The figures alone do not prove that the Basket Plus shop is closing permanently. The store had only been operating since December, meaning that 2025 represents just the beginning of its commercial activity. At the same time, the accounts show that the business was operating at a substantial loss while its revenue was still relatively modest.

The company had previously been associated with plans for further expansion, with reports indicating that as many as ten additional Hungarian stores could open within a year. For now, however, there is no official confirmation that those plans have been abandoned.

The current closure could still be temporary. But until the operator provides an explanation, the sudden disappearance of Mere’s only Hungarian store raises questions about the future of the Russian discount chain in the Hungarian market.

World.title: Hungarians rally to save energy: Minister Kapitány shares how many of us joined saving effort

István Kapitány, the economy and energy affairs minister, has welcomed that, according to surveys, 84 percent of Hungarians participated in efforts to reduce strain on the country’s energy system.

Conscious energy use helps protect the environment and manage shared resources more responsibly, the minister said. “By using energy consciously, we protect our environment, manage our shared resources more responsibly, and contribute to the country’s smooth functioning. It is worth maintaining this responsible approach in our daily lives,” he added.

World.title: Top Hungarian university’s vice-rector resigns after exam scandal that ended in lecturer’s dismissal
World.content:
Lajos György Szabó, the education vice-rector of Budapest’s Corvinus University, is stepping down from his position and leaving the institution after eight years in leadership roles. He has also promised to reveal new evidence relating to the controversial case that led to the dismissal of lecturer Zoltán Ádám.

Lajos György Szabó has announced that he is resigning as education vice-rector and will leave Corvinus University at the end of the 2025–2026 academic year. According to the university, Szabó held senior positions at the institution for eight years.

He joined Corvinus in 2016 and became vice-rector for education in 2018, later serving as general vice-rector as well. In 2023, he was appointed acting rector for one year before returning to his role as education vice-rector. His time as acting rector coincided with one of the university’s most controversial scandals in recent years.

The Zoltán Ádám case

The controversy began after a student from an influential business family was reportedly given an additional opportunity to take an examination following intervention by his parents, despite not having met the university’s requirements for sitting the exam.

Zoltán Ádám, then a lecturer at Corvinus, initiated an ethics procedure over the case. However, the affair ultimately resulted in Ádám’s dismissal from the university, with the lecturer, among other things, accused of having insulted the chancellor.

Szabó was one of the university’s key leaders at the time, serving as acting rector in 2023. He has remained in a senior position at Corvinus since then, while Belgian economist Bruno van Pottelsberghe subsequently became the university’s rector. Zoltán Ádám later publicly criticised the university’s handling of the affair, which became a major controversy surrounding Corvinus and its governance model.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

‘This is not a retreat’

In his farewell letter, Szabó stressed that his departure had been planned and was not connected to recent political changes or the controversies surrounding the university. “Obviously, there will be some who will link this to the changes of recent months,” he wrote, while insisting that he had already been considering leaving the university.

After eight years in leadership positions, Szabó said he wanted a change of environment and hoped to return to academic research. He plans to write academic papers and books. He also rejected the suggestion that his departure represented a retreat from criticism or controversy, asking colleagues who had allegedly attacked him in inappropriate terms to refrain from personal and offensive remarks.

Szabó further stressed that he had not sought to promote the foundation-based governance model itself, but rather the development of Corvinus, and said that he had never brought party politics into his work.

‘New evidence’ in the exam scandal

Despite leaving the university, Szabó indicated that the Zoltán Ádám case is not over in his view. In his farewell letter, he said that he would be prepared to make public new evidence supporting his position once he was no longer bound by confidentiality obligations.

He did not disclose what the evidence might contain, but suggested that it could shed new light on the events surrounding the examination controversy. Corvinus University has said it will soon announce who will temporarily take over Szabó’s duties as education vice-rector and his other university responsibilities.

World.title: Hungary’s euro introduction could create a major bond investment opportunity, analyst says
World.content:
Hungarian government bonds could offer significant upside if the country successfully introduces the euro, according to an analysis published by G7.

The Hungarian bond market is currently looking increasingly attractive, the analysis argues, following a sharp fall in yields after the new Tisza government came to power.

According to G7, investors have priced out some of the risks associated with the previous government, including corruption concerns, excessive spending and persistently high budget deficits. But the biggest potential catalyst could be Hungary’s declared intention to adopt the euro.

Euro adoption could trigger major bond market convergence

The analysis argues that introducing the European currency would resolve several longstanding problems for Hungary, including the population’s declining confidence in the forint.

A significant share of Hungarian household savings – reportedly close to 40 per cent – is already held in euros. The introduction of the common currency could therefore help align the country’s financial system more closely with the euro area.

Rather than focusing on the technical requirements of euro adoption, such as ERM II participation and the Maastricht criteria, G7’s analysis looks at what could happen to Hungarian government bonds if the process succeeds.

If Hungary were to adopt the common currency in around four years, as currently envisaged, bonds that are currently denominated in forints would eventually become euro-denominated assets. That could have major implications for their yields.

Hungarian yields are still well above eurozone levels

The difference can already be seen in the current government bond market. French, Italian and Greek 10-year government bond yields are currently just below 4 per cent, while Hungary’s 10-year yield stands at around 5.4 per cent.

The analysis argues that, if Hungary successfully progresses towards adoption, Hungarian yields could eventually converge towards those of other euro-denominated government bonds. This would not necessarily happen gradually or in a straight line.

Instead, the market could react strongly to major milestones such as Hungary’s 2027 budget, entry into ERM II and progress towards meeting the requirements for euro adoption.

Could Hungarian bonds deliver a double-digit gain?

G7 estimates that the yield difference between Hungarian and comparable eurozone 10-year bonds represents roughly 150 basis points of potential convergence. Because the average duration of a Hungarian 10-year government bond is around eight years, the analysis estimates that the resulting price appreciation could be approximately 12 per cent for this segment of the market.

Longer-dated bonds could offer even greater potential upside, while shorter maturities would generally have less. However, these figures are not a guaranteed return. Bond prices and yields will also depend on global interest rates, inflation, fiscal policy and investor sentiment at the time. The key argument is that successful euro adoption could create a one-off repricing event as investors reassess the risk associated with Hungarian government debt.

The biggest gains may come before the common currency arrives

Importantly, investors would not necessarily have to wait until Hungary physically adopts the euro for the potential repricing to occur. Markets typically price in future developments well before they actually happen.

As a result, major milestones could trigger successive waves of appreciation. These could include the 2027 budget, Hungary’s possible entry into ERM II and evidence that the country is successfully meeting the fiscal and economic criteria required for euro adoption.

If those developments convince investors that euro adoption is genuinely achievable, Hungarian government bonds could become increasingly attractive compared with their current valuations.

Have you read this? Hungary could introduce the euro by 2031 – but workers may pay a heavy price

Global market risks remain

The outlook is not without risks. No one can know where international bond yields will stand four years from now. Hungarian government bonds will continue to be influenced by global developed and emerging markets, as well as by international interest rates and risk appetite.

The analysis notes that global markets have become increasingly sensitive to rising government debt and weak fiscal figures in recent years. A major international market sell-off could therefore undermine the potential gains from Hungarian convergence.

Nevertheless, the analysis concludes that, assuming Hungary successfully follows through with its euro plans and international markets remain relatively stable, Hungarian government bonds could offer an unusually attractive opportunity.

For international investors, the potential combination of relatively high current yields and eventual convergence with euro-denominated bonds could make Hungarian debt particularly interesting in the years ahead.

World.title: Six taken to hospital after excess chemicals enter pool at Hungarian spa
World.content:
Six people, including two children, were taken to hospital for observation on Saturday after a large amount of chlorine entered one of the pools at the Igali Gyógyfürdő spa in southern Hungary.

The incident happened in the afternoon at the spa’s leisure pool area in Igal, Somogy County, after several visitors began feeling unwell.

Firefighters were called to the scene and inspected the area after it had been evacuated. Specialists wearing protective equipment also carried out checks, while a mobile laboratory took measurements at the site.

Four adults and two children taken to hospital

Ambulance crews examined 14 visitors following the incident. Six of them – four adults and two children – were taken to hospital for observation. There have been no reports of serious injuries.

According to Igal Mayor Imre László Szántó, the incident was caused by a technical problem that resulted in an excessive amount of chemicals entering one of the pools.

The contaminated water was treated, and the area was secured. The affected pool was subsequently closed in cooperation with the disaster management authorities, ambulance services and police.

Pool expected to remain closed until Monday

The mayor said in a video shared by Igal Média that the affected pool is likely to remain closed until Monday. However, the rest of the spa is operating normally and continues to welcome visitors.

The authorities are investigating the circumstances of the incident, while the spa is also reviewing its internal safety procedures.

Szántó said the facility would review its existing protocols and introduce changes across the spa where necessary to prevent similar incidents in the future.

World.title: Romanian shipyard delivers hull of largest cable-laying ship in Japan
World.content:
The VARD shipyard in Tulcea, eastern Romania, has completed the construction of the hull of “Discovery,” the largest vessel intended for the installation of submarine cables and the first such project delivered by the VARD group for the Japanese market.

The ship, valued at over USD 200 million, will have an important role in the development of infrastructure for offshore wind energy and the transport of electric energy through submarine cables.

The construction of the vessel’s hull was carried out in Romania, at the VARD shipyards in Tulcea and Brăila, and after launching, it was towed to the VARD Langsten shipyard in Norway, where the specialized equipment was installed, and the final tests were carried out before delivery. The vessel was officially handed over to the Japanese company Toyo Construction at the end of June and is currently heading to Japan, where it will be based in the port of Ishikari Bay.

“Discovery” was designed to meet the specific conditions in Japan, where the water depth increases rapidly near the coast. The vessel can operate both in shallow waters and offshore, where future floating wind farms will be installed.

The vessel is approximately 151 meters long, 28 meters wide, and can transport up to 9,000 tons of submarine cables, distributed in two carousels with capacities of 4,000 and 5,000 tons.

On board, the ship has a main crane with a lifting capacity of 400 tons and an auxiliary crane of 100 tons. The vessel is also equipped with a dynamic positioning system, a heliport and equipment for the operation of remotely operated underwater vehicles.

In addition to the installation of submarine cables, “Discovery” can also be used for offshore construction works, including the installation of foundations for wind turbines and anchoring operations for floating turbines.

The vessel is equipped with a hybrid propulsion system, in which diesel engines are used to produce electric energy, while propulsion is provided by electric motors. The system includes batteries and the possibility of shore power supply during stationing, in order to reduce fuel consumption and emissions. Up to 90 crew members and technicians can work on board.

The Japanese government has set the rapid expansion of offshore wind energy capacities as an objective in the coming period, and this vessel will be used for the installation of the submarine electric cables necessary to connect the new farms to the energy grid.

For VARD, the project marks the first delivery to the Japanese market in the segment of specialized vessels for the offshore wind industry. In recent years, the VARD Tulcea shipyard has specialized in the construction of the hulls of some of the most complex vessels intended for the offshore industry, including vessels for the installation of submarine cables and for the development of offshore wind energy projects.

Several of the most advanced vessels of this type currently used worldwide were built in Romania and subsequently equipped at the VARD group’s shipyards in Norway.

World.title: Romania’s eMAG to come under sole control of Naspers after EU approval
World.content:
The European Commission has approved, under the EU Merger Regulation, the acquisition of sole control over Dante International of Romania by South African investment fund Naspers Limited.

"The Commission concluded that the notified operation does not raise competition concerns, as the companies are not active on the same markets or on markets that are in a vertical relationship, and the impact on the market structure is limited. The transaction was examined under the simplified merger control procedure," the EC stated in a press release.

Last month, businessman Iulian Stanciu announced the sale of his stake in the eMAG Group to global consumer internet and technology investment group Prosus, 17 years after taking over the company and 14 years after signing the partnership with Naspers, the owner of Prosus.

After the sale, eMAG will continue its development and extensive investment plans, with RON 1.2 billion budgeted in this fiscal year alone for technology, logistics and financial services, with the support of Prosus and an experienced management team, company representatives stated. They also noted the regional growth potential of e-commerce, which remains significant, with growth rates of up to three times in the coming years, compared to the current penetration rate of 11-12% of total retail.

"The investments will be directed predominantly toward logistics and delivery infrastructure, AI and financial services, consolidating the foundation for a strong digital economy in the region. I want to thank Iulian for his dedication, vision, and for keeping us focused on the customer and on continuous personal development," said at that time Tudor Manea, CEO of eMAG Group, cited by News.ro.

At group level, eMAG recorded in fiscal year 2025 a turnover of RON 11.4 billion (USD 2.64 billion), up 11% compared with the previous financial year. The eMAG Group portfolio includes the eMAG brand, the Fashion Days online store, Romania’s 100% online hypermarket Freshful, the IT and electronics specialist store PC Garage, the Romanian national and international express courier company Sameday, the Depanero repair workshop, the most relevant recommerce platform in South-Eastern Europe Flip, as well as the financial services company HeyBlu.

World.title: Eurostat: Romania allocated only EUR 18.8 per inhabitant to R&D in 2025, lower than in 2015
World.content:
European governments allocated an estimated EUR 130.2 billion, or 0.69% of their combined GDP, to research and development in 2025, according to a Eurostat analysis published on Friday, August 7.

The sum represents an increase of 2.4% compared to 2024 (EUR 127.14 billion) and an increase of 60.5% compared to 2015 (EUR 81.13 billion).

In 2025, on average, government budget allocations for research and development at EU level amounted to EUR 288.9 per inhabitant, an increase of 57.7% compared to 2015 (EUR 183.2 per inhabitant). Luxembourg (EUR 917.2 per inhabitant) recorded the highest budget allocations for research and development per capita among the EU member countries. It was followed by Denmark (EUR 627.1) and Germany (EUR 553.5).

At the opposite end, the lowest values were recorded in Romania (EUR 18.8), Hungary (EUR 57.4) and Malta (EUR 73.7). Moreover, compared to 2015, Romania (-9.6%) was the only EU country that recorded a decrease in budget allocations for research and development expressed in euros per inhabitant, from EUR 20.8 in 2015 to EUR 18.8 in 2025.

The other EU countries recorded increases ranging from +14.7% in Sweden (from EUR 363.4 per inhabitant in 2015 to EUR 416.7 in 2025) to +495.5% in Bulgaria (from EUR 15.5 to EUR 92.3).

As regards the distribution according to socio-economic objectives, 37.3% of the amount was allocated to the general advancement of knowledge, financed mainly through a global public grant known as public general university funds, used by public higher education institutions to support their activities. In addition, 18.4% of R&D funds were allocated to the general advancement of knowledge from sources other than the general university funds, 9.5% to industrial production and technology, 6.7% to health, and 5.8% to defense.

World.title: EIB lends EUR 100 million to BRD Sogelease to increase financing for businesses in Romania
World.content:
The European Investment Bank (EIB) is lending EUR 100 million to the leasing subsidiary of BRD Groupe Société Générale to expand financing for businesses in Romania.

The goal is to facilitate financing for Romanian SMEs and Mid-Caps, which face greater hurdles in accessing long-term funding than their counterparts in many other European Union countries, EIB said.

The operation will enable BRD Sogelease to provide funding to Romanian companies seeking business expansion, productivity improvements and sustainable development.

Of the total loan, 15% is earmarked for green projects such as energy efficiency, renewable energy and sustainable transport.

Around 80% of the EIB loan is projected to be deployed in less-developed areas known in the EU as “cohesion regions.”

The new operation builds on previous EIB loans to BRD Sogelease IFN that total EUR 305 million over the past decade.

“In today’s rapidly changing economy, access to finance is a key enabler of competitiveness,” said EIB Vice-President Ioannis Tsakiris. “By partnering with BRD Sogelease, we are mobilizing investment where it matters most: among Romanian entrepreneurs. This financing will help businesses become more resilient, more innovative and better prepared for the opportunities of tomorrow.”

“Our long-standing partnership with the European Investment Bank reflects a shared commitment to supporting the growth and resilience of the Romanian economy. This new financing facility will enable us to provide SMEs and Mid-Caps with enhanced access to long-term funding on attractive terms, helping them invest in expansion, innovation, productivity and sustainable development,” said BRD Sogelease GM Gabriel Mihai.

BRD Sogelease IFN SA is the leasing subsidiary of BRD Groupe Société Générale, one of the leading banks in Romania with total assets of RON 96.3 billion as of June 2026. Established in 2001, BRD Sogelease IFN provides financial lease and other asset-based financial solutions to over 10,000 SME and Small-Cap clients in Romania.

World.title: Platform for foreign workers coming to Romania up and running, authorities say
World.content:
Romania’s Interior Ministry announced on Thursday, August 6, that the platform WorkinRomania.gov.ro is now up and running, simplifying the process of hiring foreign workers.

The platform aims to make it easier for immigrant workers to enter the domestic labor market. Among its benefits is the facilitation of the relationship between the employer and the future employee.

The platform helps both Romanian employers looking for a workforce and aids the state in managing more efficiently the employment of new workers coming from other states. “Less bureaucracy, shorter deadlines and the possibility to track each application in real time,” the Ministry noted, cited by Agerpres.

The services of this platform include: permanent access to one’s own electronic file; the possibility to track each stage of the procedure; automatic notifications regarding requests for additional documents or the adopted solutions; reduction of waiting times; increased transparency of the entire administrative process. The platform also connects future employees with the Trade Register, the Employee Records Register, as well as with IT systems for the checks provided by law.

The platform also centralizes the actions of several Romanian state institutions.

The General Inspectorate for Immigration within the Ministry of Internal Affairs handles the procedures within its competence regarding the regime of foreigners and the right of residence for employment purposes; it analyzes and resolves applications regarding the granting and extension of residence

The right of residence for employment purposes, issues the specific documents and participates in the electronic exchange of data necessary for substantiating administrative decisions.

The National Agency for Employment operationally administers the module intended for the registration and authorization of employers and agencies for the placement of foreigners and configures the workflows related to these procedures;

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through the national visa system and the eViza platform, participates in the workflows regarding the granting of long-stay visas for employment;

The National Agency for Fiscal Administration provides the information necessary for the fiscal checks provided by law;

The Ministry of Education and Research, through the National Center for the Recognition and Equivalence of Diplomas, contributes to the verification of qualifications and diplomas, in the cases provided by legislation.

The platform offers useful information for employers, placement agencies and foreign workers, available also in English. Interested persons can find on WorkinRomania.gov.ro all the information they need for creating and validating an account on the platform, the registration and authorization conditions, the necessary documents and the method of using the electronic services available on the platform.

At the same time, users have a support chat service, available both in text and voice format, which provides assistance and guidance in the use of electronic services, in Romanian and other languages.

In terms of security, the program is included in the Ministry’s Services Hub, specially designed to keep personal data safe at the level of each county.

Although Romania set an official quota of around 90,000 newly admitted foreign workers for 2026, employer demand significantly exceeds that ceiling. In some years, requests have reportedly been more than double the approved quota. Still, filling vacancies is only part of the challenge. A large share of newly arrived workers subsequently seek opportunities in other EU member states, where wages, working conditions, and social benefits are often more attractive.

World.title: Thriller starring Nicolas Cage to open this year's horror and fantastic film fest in Biertan
World.content:
The Full Moon Horror and Fantastic Film Festival, presented by the Transilvania International Film Festival, returns to Biertan for its 11th edition, bringing three days and three nights of premieres, cult films and open-air screenings.

The festival opens with the Romanian premiere of The Carpenter’s Son, starring Nicolas Cage. Another highlight of this year’s edition will be the cine-concert Trenul Fantomă, featuring live music by Dubase, preceded by an acoustic performance by Ana Coman and her guitar as part of Full Moon Unplugged.

At Bastion Open Air, the programme kicks off on Friday, August 14, with Nightborn, the new film by Finnish director Hanna Bergholm, known to horror audiences for Hatching. Selected for the competition at the Berlin International Film Festival, the film follows a couple who move into an isolated house in the Finnish woods, where the arrival of their first child awakens a disturbing presence. The evening continues with The Rocky Horror Picture Show, the horror musical that has become one of cinema’s great cult phenomena. The story behind the film will also be explored from behind the scenes in the documentary Strange Journey: The Story of Rocky Horror, screening on Saturday at Cinema Ion Hobana.

On Saturday, Bastion Open Air will screen Her Private Hell, the new film by director Nicolas Winding Refn, as well as the original Dutch version of the thriller The Vanishing. The programme also includes the 1993 American remake, also directed by George Sluizer, giving audiences an opportunity to compare the two versions.

On Sunday, Carrie returns to the Bastion screen. Directed by Brian De Palma and based on Stephen King’s novel, the classic marks 50 years since its release.

On Friday, August 14, Méliès Open Air will host the Romanian premiere of The Carpenter’s Son. Directed by Lotfy Nathan, the supernatural thriller stars Nicolas Cage as Joseph, alongside FKA twigs as Mary and Noah Jupe as their teenage son.

On Saturday, August 15, audiences are invited to the cine-concert Trenul Fantomă. Made in 1933 by Jean Mihail, the first Romanian-language talking film tells the story of travelers forced to spend the night at a railway station believed to be haunted. The film will be screened with live music performed by Dubase.

The Méliès programme concludes on Sunday, August 16, with The Virgin of the Quarry Lake, directed by Laura Casabé. Inspired by the prose of writer Mariana Enríquez, the film blends adolescence, jealousy and black magic against the backdrop of Argentina’s 2001 crisis.

The selection continues at Cinema Karloff and Cinema Ion Hobana, with titles including The Turkish Coffee Table, Gaua, Species, Roqia, Veins, The Uncertainty Principle, Feels Like Home, Anemoneciacs and Transylvania Tapes.

The program also includes Romanian short films, the documentary Strange Journey: The Story of Rocky Horror, and repeat screenings of The Carpenter’s Son, Nightborn and Her Private Hell.

The festival takes place between August 14 and August 16.

World.title: Romania’s Banca Transilvania extends EUR 71.4 mln loan for Entek Elektrik PV park
World.content:
The largest bank in Romania, Banca Transilvania, announced that it will finance the development of the Eco Sun Niculești photovoltaic park, Entek Elektrik’s first investment in local green energy production, with EUR 71.4 million.

It is one of the largest bilateral financings granted to a photovoltaic project under development in the country. Once completed, the park, located in Dâmbovița County, will have an installed capacity of approximately 205 MW. The total value of the project is estimated at EUR 100 million.

“Projects of this scale contribute to strengthening energy independence and modernizing the Romanian economy. We are pleased to support Entek Elektrik’s first investment in renewable energy production in Romania and to continue the solid partnership that we have built together,” said Cosmin Călin, Deputy General Manager Large Corporate, Banca Transilvania.

The investment in the Eco Sun Niculești project is made through Entek Elektrik Üretimi A.Ş., the renewable energy company of the Koç Group, and its main shareholder is Türkiye Petrol Refinerileri A.Ş. (Tüpraş), the largest industrial company in Turkey and the seventh largest refinery operator in Europe.

In Turkey, Entek owns an energy capacity portfolio of 550 MW. The company aims to further expand its renewable energy portfolio and seeks to become one of the leading green energy producers in Turkey.
